The paper also indicates that the controller learns benefit estimates from delayed feedback rather than relying only on static heuristics.

Implementation-wise, DynBranch sits at the model-API boundary between agent harnesses and unmodified SGLang or vLLM backends. That makes it a serving middleware design rather than a new agent runtime or a model-side method.41:T737,The main setup uses Qwen3-32B on 4×H200, with additional results on Qwen3-8B with an RTX 4090. The paper first motivates the problem empirically: in measured coding, research, and scientific agents, 45%–57% of end-to-end latency is downstream time serialized after model output. That establishes that the branch-resolution barrier is not a corner case.

On performance, DynBranch reduces mean latency by up to 32% relative to the strongest prior system for each workload on the same GPUs, and by 46%–66% relative to a no-reuse floor. When reuse is disabled and only early fill is kept, mean latency still drops by 8.5%–34.4% on model-driven paths, and user-turn latency drops by 46.6%–47.7% in human-interaction settings. This is an important result: the gains do not come only from cross-request reuse; overlapping work during the branch-resolution window already matters.

The experimental structure also suggests three points worth checking closely. First is correctness: the paper states that workflow results are preserved, consistent with the design where speculative fills become visible only after canonical authorization. Second is load sensitivity: the two-level controller should show different admission behavior under different occupancy regimes, otherwise the claim of safe speculation under load would be weak. Third is generality: the authors report that benefits persist across backbone families, which suggests the effect comes from workflow structure and serving dynamics rather than a model-specific artifact.

The provided text does not include the full result tables, so it is not safe to invent more workload-level absolute latency or hit-rate numbers. But the central empirical message is clear: the combination of reuse, early fill, and load-aware admission outperforms caching-only or speculation-only baselines.42:T525,The framework maximizes draft-token acceptance subject to an f-divergence constraint between the mentored output distribution and the target distribution. The total-variation case is used as a warm-up and has a clean geometric structure: the set of optimal solutions is the intersection of a coordinate-wise hyperrectangle induced by the drafter and target, the probability simplex, and the active divergence boundary. This set is large enough to contain the optimal solutions for all strictly convex f-divergences. For a general strictly convex f-divergence, the optimal mentored distribution is unique and has a coordinate-wise clamping form, π* = max{αq, min{p, βq}}, where q is the target distribution, p is the drafter distribution, and 0 ≤ α < 1 < β. Intuitively, each token probability is kept within lower and upper multiplicative bands around the target probability, while moving along a one-dimensional path from the target toward the drafter. A notable property is that this path does not depend on the chosen f-divergence. The paper further connects the composite output distribution to boosting by developing a multiclass extension of self-normalized boosting and by showing how the drafter-target mixture can satisfy boosting-style conditions when the two models have useful edge complementarity.43:T91f,方法核心是 acoustic-to-text KV compression。基础模型是 MiniCPM-o 4.5，它按 1 秒为单位处理 duplex unit，每个 unit 内包含音频 token、一个 native 的 <|listen|> 或 <|speak|> 决策，以及后续可能的响应生成。作者在每个 unit 的第一个 native decision 之后，插入一个可选的 transcription segment，用新引入的 <|asr_start|> 和 <|asr_end|> 包围。这个 segment 只作为语言模型上下文中的文本记忆存在，不送入 speech decoder，也不会被说出来。

推理时，模型自己决定是否打开 side channel。如果预测出 <|asr_start|>，就贪心解码最多 64 个文本 token，直到 <|asr_end|>；若超长或遇到控制 token，则强制闭合。随后，当 resident KV cache 超过目标预算时，系统驱逐更早的 acoustic states，但保留这些 transcript token，并保留一个最近的 acoustic window 以覆盖转写延迟。于是，较老的语音内容以文本形式留在上下文里，最近一段仍保留原始声学细节，形成“远处文本化、近处声学化”的混合记忆。

训练上，作者没有单独接一个 ASR 模型，而是复用原有 LM backbone，只用 LoRA 适配 side channel。监督信号来自带词级强制对齐的转写数据：每个词根据其声学结束时间和额外延迟 δ 被分配到某个 1 秒 unit 中，每个词只出现在一个目标 transcription segment。仅用 transcription cross-entropy 会改变原模型的原生对话行为，所以作者再加入 token-level knowledge distillation。具体做法是：冻结原始 full-duplex 模型作为 teacher，让它在同一音频上、但不插入 transcription segment 地运行；收集 teacher 在所有 native prediction positions 的全词表分布；student 在插入 transcription segment 的序列上训练时，对这些 native 位置同时拟合 teacher 分布。这样 side channel 学会转写，同时尽量不扰动原有 listen/speak 决策、停顿处理、打断响应等行为。

这个设计和“单独训练一个流式 ASR，再把文本喂回模型”相比，有两个差异。其一，推理时不需要额外 ASR 模块，部署更简单；其二，蒸馏约束的是 full-duplex 原生行为，而不只是转写准确率，因此目标更贴近语音对话模型的系统需求。44:T828,实验围绕三件事展开：KV 峰值控制、长时语音理解、实时性与交互行为保持。主模型是 MiniCPM-o 4.5。作者指出，转写后的文本记忆大约每秒只占 3 个序列位置，而原始 acoustic history 约占 17 个位置，这给压缩上限提供了直观背景。

在十分钟 LongSpeech session 上，与“同样经过 side-channel 适配但不做 eviction”的模型相比，峰值 streaming KV cache 大小下降 64.6%。这说明收益主要来自“文本化后驱逐旧声学 KV”，而不是仅仅插入 transcript token。长时理解方面，论文称该方法在 transcription、temporal question answering、summarization 上都优于 native streaming，说明文本记忆不仅节省显存，也改善了对长程语言内容的保持。

实时性方面，在 4K KV cache budget 下，包含 transcription 与 cache eviction 在内的整套处理，在 H100、batch size 1 上对每个 1 秒音频单元平均耗时 461 ms；在 10,039 个 unit 的测量中没有 deadline miss。这一点很关键，因为方法成立的前提就是 side channel 能在 listening-time slack 内完成。若超过 1 秒窗口，就会破坏 full-duplex 实时性。

行为保持方面，Full-Duplex-Bench 上 pause-handling、turn-taking、interruption 等指标与原模型相当，支持了蒸馏约束确实在抑制 side-channel 训练对原生交互行为的扰动。摘要还提到 WER 统计会把 skipped/truncated segments 计入错误，这意味着作者没有通过只评估成功打开 side channel 的片段来美化结果。

从方法设计推断，值得关注的消融应包括：只做 CE 转写监督、不做 KD 时 native behavior 的退化；不同 KV budget 下理解与实时性的折中；recent acoustic window 大小对性能的影响；以及 emission delay δ 对转写完整性和驱逐时机的影响。给出的全文片段没有完整表格数字，但主结论已经足够明确：在线文本化旧语音上下文，可以在不破坏 full-duplex 交互的前提下显著降低峰值 KV，并提升长时理解。45:T95a,The core method is acoustic-to-text KV compression. The base model, MiniCPM-o 4.5, processes interaction in 1-second duplex units. Each unit contains audio tokens, a native <|listen|> or <|speak|> decision, and possibly response generation. After the first native decision in each unit, the authors insert an optional transcription segment delimited by two new tokens, <|asr_start|> and <|asr_end|>. This segment stays in the language-model context as textual memory, but it is excluded from the speech decoder input and from spoken output.

At inference time, the model decides whether to open the side channel. If it predicts <|asr_start|>, it greedily decodes up to 64 text tokens until <|asr_end|>; if the segment overruns or hits a control token, the segment is forcibly closed. When the resident KV cache exceeds a target budget, older acoustic states are evicted while transcript tokens are retained, together with a recent acoustic window that covers transcription delay. The resulting memory is hybrid: older context is preserved in text form, while recent context remains acoustically grounded.

Training avoids a separate ASR model. The side channel is adapted with LoRA on top of the existing LM backbone. Supervision comes from transcribed utterances with word-level forced alignment. Each word is assigned to a 1-second unit based on its acoustic endpoint plus an additional emission delay delta, and each word appears in exactly one target transcription segment. However, pure transcription cross-entropy would alter the model's native conversational behavior. To prevent that, the paper adds token-level knowledge distillation. A frozen teacher, namely the original full-duplex model without transcription segments, processes the same audio. Its full-vocabulary distributions at native prediction positions are collected, and the student is trained to match them at those positions while also learning the inserted transcription segments. This constrains changes to native listen/speak decisions, pause handling, interruption behavior, and response generation.

Compared with a pipeline that runs a separate streaming ASR and feeds text back into the model, this design has two practical differences. It removes the need for an extra ASR module at inference, and it regularizes the adapted model toward preserving full-duplex behavior rather than optimizing transcription alone.46:T989,The experiments focus on three aspects: peak KV control, long-form speech understanding, and real-time behavioral preservation. The base model is MiniCPM-o 4.5. The paper notes that transcript memory uses roughly 3 sequence positions per second of speech, versus about 17 for acoustic history, which gives a clear intuition for why the compression can matter.

On 10-minute LongSpeech sessions, peak streaming KV cache size is reduced by 64.6% relative to the same side-channel-adapted model without eviction. This is an important comparison because it isolates the gain from converting old acoustic context into text and then evicting acoustic KV, rather than from simply inserting transcript tokens. On long-form understanding, the method improves transcription, temporal question answering, and summarization over native streaming, suggesting that textual memory is not only cheaper but also more effective for retaining long-range linguistic content.

On real-time feasibility, under a 4K KV-cache budget the full processing path, including transcription and cache eviction, averages 461 ms per 1-second audio unit on an H100 at batch size 1. Across 10,039 measured units, there are no deadline misses. This matters because the whole method depends on finishing side-channel work within the listening-time slack.

On behavioral preservation, results on Full-Duplex-Bench show comparable pause handling, turn taking, and interruption performance. That supports the claim that token-level distillation successfully constrains the side-channel adaptation. The paper also states that skipped or truncated transcription segments are counted as errors in WER, which is a useful detail because it avoids reporting only successful side-channel openings.

The most informative ablations are likely the following: cross-entropy-only transcription training versus CE plus KD, to show how native behavior degrades without distillation; different KV budgets to expose the trade-off between memory and understanding; the size of the retained recent acoustic window; and the effect of the emission delay delta on transcription completeness and eviction timing. If you only want to judge transferability to another speech LM, read the method figure, the training objective, and the real-time result under the 4K budget.48:T7d2,The method has three layers. First, the paper builds an error model for MLA dual-path quantization. MLA stores a shared low-rank content latent and a decoupled RoPE key cache. Quantization errors in the content path propagate through attention matching, value aggregation, and their interaction. Errors in the RoPE path enter mainly through the RoPE-induced QK logit term. Across six models from four families, the authors show that under matched cache reconstruction error, RoPE-path quantization causes substantially larger attention-output distortion. They then explain this with an operator–error model based on attention sensitivity to logits, how quantization error energy is allocated across subspaces, and how error directions couple with sensitive operator directions.

Second, they propose QuantMLA, a function-aligned dual-path quantization framework. The key design choice is not to use one shared quantization objective. Instead, each path gets its own offline-fusible transformation space and its own functional target. For the content path, the objective is attention-output reconstruction: optimize the quantized representation so that the downstream attention output is preserved, rather than merely reconstructing the latent tensor. For the RoPE path, the objective is positional QK reconstruction: directly preserve the position-sensitive QK term, since that is the main route through which RoPE errors affect outputs. The paper also derives a theoretical bound linking this objective to output distortion.

Third, the paper includes a native low-bit MLA attention backend. Unpacking and dequantization are fused into the attention computation instead of restoring high-precision tensors first. This matters because cache compression only translates into real serving gains if bandwidth and intermediate memory traffic are reduced at execution time. The evaluation therefore includes not only kernel-level behavior but also end-to-end vLLM serving under the same scheduling policy.49:T5cf,The analysis spans six models from four MLA families, with total model sizes ranging from 16B to 1T parameters. The main empirical results are threefold.

First, the paper reports what it describes as the first joint INT4 caching result for both the content cache and the RoPE cache in MLA, with only minor accuracy degradation. That is the central quality result, because prior MLA quantization work largely avoided low-bit RoPE caching. Second, in a more aggressive setting, it further compresses the content cache to INT2 while keeping the RoPE cache at INT4, and still maintains competitive performance on difficult reasoning and coding benchmarks. This supports the paper’s main analysis: the content path is materially more compressible than the RoPE path. Third, on the systems side, it reports up to 3.59× KV-cache compression at 128K context length and up to 5.168× whole-job output throughput relative to BF16 in the evaluated cache-pressure workload under the same native vLLM scheduling policy.

The most useful ablations are not just score tables. They establish a chain of evidence: matched reconstruction error does not imply matched functional distortion; path-specific objectives outperform generic reconstruction objectives; and a native low-bit backend is necessary to realize the memory savings as actual throughput gains. DFlash processes an anchor token plus M masked draft positions in one pass and conditions on target-model context features, but predecessor information is weak or delayed. The paper first shows that early draft positions already contain recoverable token-predictive information in shallow layers, and that successor accuracy depends strongly on both the adjacent predecessor content and the depth at which that information is introduced. DSpine uses a gated adjacent injection module at every layer: each position writes its predicted feature into the next position, so the causal chain unfolds over network depth while all draft positions are updated in parallel. The method also builds a unified transfer space from the target model’s output embeddings, aligning layer-wise injection with predecessor-conditioned decoding. Layer-wise output-embedding supervision encourages shallow layers to form transferable predictive features. A transition cache precomputes adjacent candidate-pair scores in parallel, reducing the sequential cost of conditional decoding.4d:T469,LatentSift replaces the first-stage LLM-based execution-free verifier in a hybrid SWE verification pipeline. The standard pipeline scores all K trajectories with an EF verifier, keeps a subset, then applies regression tests, LLM-generated tests, and a final EF selection step. LatentSift instead collects hidden states while the policy is generating candidates, adding no extra LLM tokens. It represents each trajectory through three channels: reasoning states, environment-observation states, and function-call states. During training, states from successful and unsuccessful trajectories are stored in positive and negative banks. At inference time, candidate states are compared with these banks, step-level distance margins are aggregated, and channel-level ranks are fused conservatively so that a candidate must look good across the behavioral channels. A separate linear scorer trained on policy hidden states produces a learned trajectory score. The final filtering score combines normalized ranks from the distance branch and the learned scorer, then retains half of the candidates for the remaining verification stages.4e:T91b,方法由三部分组成，分别对应作者提出的三个瓶颈。

第一部分是 path-aware tile routing。DFlash 原生实现对 prefill 和 verify 复用同一套 attention tile 选择逻辑，但两者 query length 分布完全不同：prefill 往往很长，verify 只有短 candidate block。沿用 prefill 的 tile 会让 verify 阶段出现大量无效 padding。DScale 为不同执行路径选择预编译 tile，使 verify 使用更贴合短序列 workload 的 tile 形状，同时保留 prefill 的复用收益。这里的关键不是新 attention 算法，而是把“prefill 和 verify 是两种不同 kernel workload”显式编码进图选择逻辑。

第二部分是 dynamic verify-length, DVL。作者不去缩短 drafter 的生成长度，而是在验证前决定每个请求实际送多少 candidate prefix 进入 target verify graph。为此训练了一个很小的 predictor，参数量只有 112K，针对 target–drafter pair 学一次即可。它不做概率校准，也不需要硬件 profile，只输出用于排序/分配的分数。系统在共享预算下给不同请求分配不同 verify-length，并把总 candidate-slot 容量压到 native verify graph 的一半左右。这样做的动机很清楚：真正值得 target 花算力验证的，是更可能形成长 accepted prefix 的请求；对低潜力请求，保留完整 draft 但少送一些位置去 verify，比一刀切截断所有请求更划算。

第三部分是 fixed-address compact workspace。DVL 之后，每个请求的 prefix 边界会动态变化，这与 CUDA graph 偏好的 fixed-shape 接口冲突。DScale 用固定地址工作区来承载压缩后的 token、边界和前缀信息，让 decision graph、verify graph 和 acceptance 逻辑共享这些动态边界，同时继续复用 captured graphs，而不需要 CPU 侧重新切片。论文里 flat-pack compaction 是这里的配套机制：把各请求选中的 prefix 紧凑排布进共享验证预算，尽量保留长前缀，减少 padding 和空槽。

整体上，DScale 的思路不是改 acceptance rule，也不是训练更强 drafter，而是把 verify 当成一个受预算约束的 packing 和调度问题。相比 DSpark 这类依赖 confidence calibration 和硬件曲线的方法，它更轻量，也更容易迁移到已有 DFlash 部署上。4f:T9d9,The method has three main components, each tied to one of the identified bottlenecks.

First, path-aware tile routing. Native DFlash uses the same attention-tile selection logic for prefill and verification, even though the workloads are structurally different: prefill has long query lengths, while verification operates on short candidate blocks. Reusing prefill-oriented tiles in verification leaves many inactive positions and wastes work. DScale introduces path-specific routing over precompiled tiles so that verification uses tile shapes better matched to short-query execution, while prefill still benefits from its own optimized path. This is not a new attention algorithm; it is a workload-aware graph-selection strategy.

Second, dynamic verify-length allocation (DVL). Instead of shortening the drafter’s output, DScale decides how many candidate positions from each request should actually enter the target verification graph. A tiny predictor—112K parameters, trained once per target–drafter pair—produces scores for allocation. The predictor does not require confidence calibration and does not depend on hardware speed-curve preparation. Under a shared verification budget, requests with higher expected acceptance potential receive longer verified prefixes, while lower-value prefixes are trimmed. The total candidate-slot budget is reduced to roughly half of the native verification capacity. The point is to spend target-model verification on prefixes likely to yield longer accepted runs, rather than uniformly truncating every request.

Third, a fixed-address compact workspace. DVL makes request boundaries dynamic, which conflicts with fixed-shape graph replay. DScale introduces a compact workspace that stores packed tokens, boundaries, and prefix metadata at fixed addresses, allowing the decision graph, verification graph, and acceptance logic to share changing boundaries while still reusing captured graphs. Flat-pack compaction is the associated packing mechanism: selected prefixes from different requests are laid out densely under the shared budget, preserving long useful prefixes and reducing padding without CPU-side re-slicing.

Overall, DScale treats verification as a budgeted packing and scheduling problem. It does not modify the acceptance rule and does not depend on a stronger drafter. Compared with approaches such as DSpark that rely on confidence calibration and hardware profiling, it is lighter-weight and easier to layer onto an existing DFlash-style deployment.50:T60e,The evaluation spans four datasets, two target models, and concurrency levels from 8 to 32 on A100-40GB with tensor parallelism 1. Relative to DFlash, DScale improves geometric-mean throughput by 43.9% to 48.8% and reduces aggregate mean end-to-end latency by 31.4% to 33.1%. On GSM8K, GPU profiling shows 30.8% to 52.5% shorter complete decode steps.

A particularly informative intermediate metric is accepted-token retention. If verification capacity is reduced without a good allocation policy, only about 71% of accepted tokens are retained. With budget adjustment, retention rises to above 91%. That result matters because it shows the gain is not simply from verifying fewer tokens; it comes from verifying fewer low-value tokens while preserving most generation progress.

The ablations are the strongest part of the empirical section. The paper presents cumulative ablations showing that path-aware tiles, predictor scoring, budget allocation, and packing/workspace each add incremental benefit rather than one trick dominating the outcome. Runtime overhead is also small: prediction, budget allocation, and packing together account for only 3.08% to 4.08% of step time in GPU execution at concurrency 8. The motivation section provides the key baseline profile: for Qwen3-8B with an approximately 1B, five-layer DFlash drafter on GSM8K at concurrency 16, 83.3% of summed GPU-kernel time is spent in the target verification graph, versus 10.9% in the draft graph. That profile explains why verification-side optimization is the right target.51:T4b7,Read this as a systems paper about where block-diffusion decoding actually spends time. Estimated reading time: 25–35 minutes.52:T6ee,The method, BASE, stands for Batch-Aware Selection of Experts using Predicted Removal Error. For token t, the MoE output is y_t = sum_{u in R_t} w_{t,u} E_u(z_t). If some experts are not loaded at the batch level, the layer output changes. The paper writes the resulting squared error as a sum of individual removal terms plus cross terms between experts omitted together. The key claim is that selection is robust to dropping the cross terms, which makes it possible to score experts independently and keep the highest-scoring ones under a fixed budget.

The score is a predicted removal error. For a token-expert pair, the removal cost is tied to the squared router weight and the expert output energy ||E_u(z_t)||^2. The difficulty is that the true expert output is unavailable before the expert is fetched and executed, while selection must happen beforehand. BASE addresses this by training a lightweight linear predictor for each expert during calibration. At inference time, it predicts the expert’s output energy from the current token representation, combines that with router weights, aggregates the resulting costs across the batch, and selects the experts with the largest predicted batch-level impact.

The paper also handles the practical case where a token routes to an expert that was not loaded. It uses a backfill mechanism, replacing the missing expert with an available routed alternative. Compared with methods such as SERE and OEA, which build the batch active set more directly from token routing decisions, BASE asks a stronger question: how much does this expert matter to the current batch output? Compared with ExFold, which relies on calibrated expert norms, BASE uses token-conditioned predictions rather than static expert strength estimates.53:T44f,The evaluation spans three MoE architectures and eight benchmarks, with comparisons under different batch budgets. The headline results reported in the paper are strong in the tight-budget regime: BASE improves average accuracy by 3.0 to 29.5 points over prior batch-aware decoding methods at comparable speed. Under more relaxed budgets, it stays within 0.4 points of dense or full-MoE quality while delivering 22% to 60% higher throughput.

The most important experimental checks are likely the ablations behind the method assumptions. One is the effect of dropping cross terms in the removal-error objective; the paper argues this has little impact on the selected expert set. Another is the quality of the output-energy predictor. If a simple linear model is sufficient, that suggests expert output energy is predictable enough from token representations to make the online procedure practical. Any plots showing how the batch-wise expert union grows with batch size, and how BASE controls that growth under a budget, are especially informative because they directly justify the problem formulation.54:T45c,The main idea is a serving virtualization layer that separates the skipping policy from engine execution. A skipper exposes per-token RUN or Project-Only decisions at routed layers. vSkipper then realizes those decisions inside SGLang while preserving the engine’s batching and cache interfaces. RUN rows execute the layer normally. Project-Only rows bypass the layer’s attention and FFN, but still write the KV state needed by future autoregressive attention. This KV-complete treatment is the key correctness constraint: skipping hidden-state computation does not mean the layer can disappear from the cache. For execution, vSkipper packs rows with the same decision into cohorts at each routed layer, runs the corresponding computation, and scatters outputs back to the original batch positions. It also uses profitability-aware mode switching, routing only when estimated savings exceed the overhead of routing, packing, and dispatch. This differs from research implementations that route every step through specialized generation loops and often lose the saved compute to control-flow and batching overhead.55:T7a3,SCSP changes the extraction pipeline rather than the model weights. The method has four components.

First, the document is partitioned into sentence-aware chunks, each capped at a maximum token length. This is not only for tractability. It narrows the semantic scope of the later compression prompt so that token-importance estimation happens in a more coherent local context.

Second, a short semantic-compression prompt such as “Brief summary: \"” is appended to each chunk. The prompt is not used to generate summaries explicitly. Instead, it is meant to trigger the model’s internal compression behavior, so that the prompt token’s attention pattern reflects which tokens in the chunk matter most semantically. The punctuation choice is deliberate: the colon and opening quote reduce the chance that the next-token distribution collapses onto punctuation continuation rather than semantic compression.

Third, the authors introduce a prompt-isolated attention mask. This mask prevents later document tokens from attending to the inserted prompts, which avoids contaminating the original document-token representations. At the same time, each prompt is restricted to attend only within its own chunk, so the resulting attention pattern is a local importance signal rather than a globally entangled one.

Fourth, token importance is estimated from the prompt-induced attention distributions, informative tokens are selected, and their representations from an intermediate layer are selectively pooled into the final embedding. Two design choices matter here. The method uses an intermediate layer rather than the final layer, consistent with the common observation that final layers in generative LLMs are often less suitable for semantic embedding geometry. And SCSP is designed as a plug-in on top of existing training-free methods such as Echo, TP, and HTP, so it complements prior work on backward information flow rather than replacing it.56:T537,From the available full-text excerpt, the main empirical claim is that SCSP consistently improves several training-free long-context embedding baselines across multiple benchmarks, and can also further improve fine-tuned embedding models. The compared baselines include Echo, Token Prepending (TP), and Hierarchical Token Prepending (HTP). The gain is attributed to selective aggregation rather than another mechanism for fixing causal information flow.

The most important ablations are likely the following. First, sentence-aware chunking versus naive fixed-length chunking: if sentences are split arbitrarily, the compression prompt should produce noisier importance estimates. Second, the prompt-isolated mask: without isolation, the inserted prompts can interfere with document-token representations and reduce the benefit. Third, the token-selection ratio, the chosen extraction layer, and selective pooling versus mean pooling: these determine whether the method is truly benefiting from better token choice rather than from prompt insertion alone.

The provided excerpt does not include the full result tables or exact benchmark scores, so no specific numbers are claimed here. What is clear is the intended positioning: training-free, modular, and especially useful when long documents contain substantial semantic redundancy.57:T483,HeadGuard is a protection layer on top of an existing KV-cache quantizer, not a replacement quantization algorithm. Model weights stay in BF16. Text keys and values also stay in BF16. For image-token KV entries, unprotected heads are handled by the base quantizer, while selected image keys, or both keys and values, bypass quantization and remain in BF16. The selection is done offline. During calibration, two differentiable scalar gates are attached to each query head. The image gate scales the post-softmax attention weights on image-token columns without renormalization, measuring sensitivity of the correct-answer log probability to the image contribution. The output gate scales the whole head output and measures sensitivity through prompt-token next-token cross-entropy. The method uses mean absolute gradients as local first-order scores. For grouped-query attention, query-head scores are averaged into physical KV-head scores. Image-sensitivity and output-sensitivity scores are standardized, added, and the top-K physical KV heads are protected. The main experiments use roughly one eighth of all physical KV heads as the protection budget.58:T424,The evaluation covers eight VLMs, three base quantizers, and eight benchmarks. The models include LLaVA-1.5-7B, LLaVA-NeXT-Mistral-7B, Qwen2.5-VL-7B, Qwen2-VL-2B, Gemma-3-12B, Gemma-4-12B, Pixtral-12B, and InternVL3-8B. The discriminative tasks are POPE, MME, MMBench, image-based ScienceQA, multiple-choice MMMU, and SEED-Bench. TextVQA and COCO captioning are used for free-form generation. By default, head scores are computed from 100 labeled POPE examples per model and then reused across tasks and base quantizers. One diagnostic result is that per-token 2-bit min-max KV quantization gives 0.832 POPE accuracy for LLaVA-NeXT but only 0.496 for Qwen2.5-VL under the same protocol, showing large model-dependent robustness differences. HeadGuard recovers more performance when the base quantizer is weak and the bit width is low, with stronger gains reported for Qwen and InternVL. The paper also studies key-only versus key-and-value protection, head-budget sweeps, calibration choices, and the added value of image-sensitivity beyond output-sensitivity.59:T43b,ARC-KV keeps the reconstruction-based formulation of methods such as Attention Matching, but amortizes the costly anchor discovery step. It first trains a value-aware indexer that scores real keys using reference activations, reference queries, and the cached KV pairs. The indexer is trained against held-out post-fitting attention-output fidelity, with disjoint scoring, fitting, and holdout queries, rather than supervised by OMP-selected anchors. After anchors are chosen, deterministic merging groups keys by their response profiles to reference queries and moves each anchor toward the mass-weighted centroid of its group, so non-anchor information is partially absorbed while the compact key remains constrained. Finally, with compact keys fixed, the method solves for the mass bias β and compact values C_v in closed form for the current context. This differs from eviction methods because discarded tokens can still influence the reconstructed cache, and differs from OMP-based AM because only the selection prior is amortized while reconstruction remains context-specific.5a:T422,The authors formulate PTQ as approximating a linear layer under a layer-wise reconstruction loss with round-to-nearest quantization. Their central result states that, for i.i.d. Gaussian weights and calibration activations with sufficiently large effective rank, the normalized RTN reconstruction loss converges uniformly over scales to a deterministic scalar objective: the mean-squared error of uniformly quantizing a standard Gaussian variable. They then analyze this limiting objective. It has a unique nondegenerate optimal scale, and the optimal scale decreases as quantizer resolution increases. They also study a scale-invariant curvature that captures local sensitivity around the optimum and observe that it decays roughly exponentially with bit-width. The paper connects this analysis to Hadamard incoherence processing, which spreads weight magnitudes through a random orthogonal transform and makes transformed weights closer to Gaussian. It also introduces Proxy-static, a computationally cheaper GPTQ-aware proxy objective for choosing scales.5b:T53c,The framework has two components. The first is Anchor-Label Relabelling, or ALR. Instead of using the original corpus token as the label for every drafted slot, ALR relabels slots using distributions derived from greedy rollouts of the target model. This restores valid supervision after divergence because the labels now correspond to what the target would generate under the actual context reached during rollout. In effect, ALR replaces invalid corpus continuations with target-consistent labels.

The second component is In-Rollout Anchors, or IRA. Relabelling alone does not fully solve the mismatch if the drafter is still mostly trained on corpus contexts rather than target-generated contexts. IRA inserts draft blocks directly into target rollouts, exposing the drafter to contexts that the target model actually visits while also reusing prefix computation. This reduces train-test mismatch and improves efficiency.

An important detail is that the paper treats erase-style methods as serious baselines, not strawmen. The comparison includes soft survival-weighted erase from prior work, and the appendix notes that soft gating is stronger than matched ungated distillation. Relative to these baselines, ALR recovers labels, while IRA recovers context. The combined method addresses both invalid supervision and exposure mismatch.5c:T646,The experiments cover both text and vision-language targets. On text benchmarks with Qwen3-4B, the average speedup over seven tasks at T=0 improves from 2.35x for DFlash, 2.67x for Erase, and 2.70x for ALR to 2.80x for ALR+IRA. The corresponding accepted-length metric tau improves from 3.32, 3.75, and 3.87 to 3.93. At T=1, the average speedups are 2.23x, 2.45x, 2.48x, and 2.55x, with tau values 3.10, 3.46, 3.56, and 3.60. Gains are especially visible on reasoning and coding tasks. For example at T=0, HumanEval improves from 3.46x with Erase to 3.63x with ALR+IRA, AIME25 from 3.01x to 3.14x, and GSM8K from 3.16x to 3.55x. On vision-language settings, Table 1 and Figure 2 show that ALR+IRA achieves the best accepted length across multiple 8B and 4B configurations. Compared with DFlash trained on the same data, ALR+IRA improves accepted length by up to 36.5% at T=0 and 33.1% at T=1 across the two 8B settings. If you work on serving or drafter training, spend another 30 minutes on the appendices to understand the baseline definitions and evaluation protocol.5e:T857,The system, Galahad, has two separable components. Taliesin stores and restores the KV state produced by prefilling a block of text. Blaise stores the text itself in sectioned form and selects a relevant section on the CPU so the model reads only that section rather than the full corpus. Taliesin removes repeated computation; Blaise removes unnecessary reading.

Taliesin is built around byte-exact memory. After a runtime computes KV state for a prompt block, the system stores that state under a fingerprint defined by the exact input bytes, the model fingerprint, and the tenant identity. If a later request contains the same byte block, the runtime loads the saved KV state instead of recomputing it. The design goal is exactness: restored state must yield bit-identical logits to a fresh prefill. To enforce this, the system validates stored records on load and falls back to normal computation on any failure. The guiding rule is explicit: serve without memory rather than serve with wrong memory. This differs from approximate cache reuse or ordinary GPU prefix caching, where the emphasis is often hit rate rather than strict equivalence.

Blaise is retrieval-like, but the returned unit is byte-exact text rather than an approximate semantic chunk assembled from embeddings. The paper does not disclose the internal section-selection method. It reports only the first operating mode, where the CPU selects one section and passes its exact text to the model. A second mode is mentioned, where the model reads Blaise’s index and Taliesin amortizes that reading too, but that mode is not evaluated here.

Implementation-wise, Galahad is packaged as a shared library that plugs into vLLM, SGLang, and llama.cpp without modifying model weights or runtime source code. It requires tenant identity and model fingerprinting to prevent cross-model or cross-tenant misuse, supports integrity checks and encryption at rest, and explains why reuse must happen at block granularity with exact token-position alignment. That boundary follows from transformer positional structure and KV semantics: near matches are not safe substitutes.5f:T662,The evaluation has two main parts: correctness and system behavior. The most important result is not a benchmark score but exact restoration. The authors report bit-identical logits after save-and-restore and byte-equal prefill across four model architectures. They also test four safety mechanisms—confirmation hash, licence signature, tenant separation, and byte comparison on load—using explicit attack toggles: attacks succeed when the defense is disabled and fail when it is enabled. This makes correctness a first-class requirement rather than a best-effort property.

On workload analysis, the paper reports that across seven real-world datasets, 98.7% of prompt tokens were text the model had already read before. That number is the main justification for persistent memory: if nearly all prompt tokens are repeated, prefill reuse can dominate latency and energy savings.

In a controlled recall test, Blaise reduces the text passed per question from roughly 97,000 tokens to about 668 tokens by selecting one relevant section instead of sending the full corpus. The introduction also states that the paper measures accuracy, latency, and GPU energy, includes an external retrieval baseline, and covers 30 out of 30 tested models, but the provided full-text excerpt does not include the complete result tables. The most concrete confirmed findings are therefore exact restoration, very high repeated-token rates, and large context reduction from section-level text selection.

From a research perspective, the two numbers to remember are 98.7% repeated prompt tokens and the 97k-to-668 token reduction in the recall setup.60:T40c,For a skim, start with the problem reframing in the introduction: the point is not to make the model read better, but to stop paying repeatedly for reading the same bytes. The bit-identical logits, byte-equal prefill, and fail-closed fallback policy are what determine whether this is deployable infrastructure or just a systems idea.

Estimated reading time is 20 to 30 minutes. The highest-density sections are the system-boundary discussion and the correctness checks.61:T6a5,UBTree has two main ideas. The first is architectural factorization. Drafting is split into a unigram proposer, a bigram selector, and a tree constructor. The proposer is a block-parallel drafter in the DFlash style: it predicts candidate tokens for all positions in a drafting block independently, preserving the throughput advantage of parallel drafting. The selector then scores adjacent candidate-token pairs instead of restoring full autoregressive dependence. It uses proposer hidden states together with frozen target embeddings transformed by separate MLPs into predecessor and successor representations, and predicts transition scores for candidate pairs. The method also learns depth-dependent weights to combine proposer logits with selector scores, which effectively lets shallow tree levels rely more on marginal token quality and deeper levels rely more on local path consistency. The second idea is tree-native training. Instead of standard distillation on target rollouts sampled at inference temperature, UBTree uses high-temperature regenerated target trajectories and a renormalized KL objective. High-temperature trajectories expose more plausible alternatives beyond the top path, while renormalized KL focuses supervision on these meaningful alternatives rather than wasting signal on low-quality tail mass. The result is a drafter trained not just to produce one strong path, but to allocate probability mass across multiple branches that are useful for tree verification. Compared with prior tree drafting methods, the contribution is not merely “using a tree”; it is explicitly matching both model structure and training objective to the multi-branch verification setting.62:T432,The paper evaluates UBTree on both academic-scale and production-scale settings. The headline result reported in the introduction is an average decoding speedup of 5.84× to 6.94× over autoregressive decoding on Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B, together with longer acceptance lengths. On a production model, Ling3-Flash-124B, UBTree is described as competitive with frontier baselines such as DSpark. The paper also emphasizes stronger durability on long-context tasks and in high-entropy scenarios, which is exactly where single-path parallel drafters tend to degrade. From the method description, the key ablations are likely to show that removing the bigram selector hurts branch quality, replacing tree-native training with standard single-path training reduces the usefulness of lower-ranked branches, and depth-dependent score fusion improves node ranking across tree levels. The full numeric tables are not present in the provided excerpt, but the text makes it clear that gains come from both the architectural change and the training objective, not from one isolated trick.63:T40c,The main value for pretraining and multimodal foundation-model research is not just the pruning recipe itself, but the interface insight it reveals. First, encoder outputs already contain a strong signal about how the downstream LM will use audio tokens. That matters for audio tokenization, projector design, and encoder–decoder co-training. Second, the work shifts compression from inside the LM to before the LM, which is the only place where one saves both compute and context budget. That makes the result relevant to long-audio modeling and unified multimodal context allocation. Third, the finding that future all-layer attention is linearly decodable from encoder representations suggests a stable linear structure between encoder features and LM usage. That opens up natural follow-ups: auxiliary pretraining losses, distillation targets, or tokenizer learning objectives aligned with downstream LM salience. This is not a new modeling paradigm, but it is a useful systems-and-representation result with clear transfer value.64:T7e2,The method is simple, and the paper’s strength is in how carefully the problem is framed and validated. For each audio token i, the authors define a target score g_i: the total attention the token receives from audio positions, summed over all heads and all layers of the language model. In their prompt format, the question comes after the audio, so under causal attention the audio positions never see the question. That means g_i is independent of the question and can be used for pre-question pruning.

The key empirical finding is that g_i can be predicted from the encoder output e_i with a linear map, s_i = w^T e_i + b. This predictor, called the prior, is fit in closed form and does not require labels or a separately trained neural predictor. Triage then uses a two-stage pruning strategy. Stage 1 prunes before the LM runs, using the prior ranking; this is the stage that saves both prefilling cost and context slots. Stage 2 is used for multiple-choice settings: after two LM layers, the method refines the ranking using observed attention and prunes again. Importantly, the paper argues that for audio, mid-LM pruning should be a correction step rather than the main mechanism, because early-layer attention is still high and early rankings are not yet reliable.

Several technical details matter. The paper compares the prior against other signals available before the LM runs—position, loudness, self-information, encoder attention, and related waveform/word properties—and finds they are much weaker predictors of future LM attention. It also performs controlled analyses showing that after accounting for position and other confounds, the prior retains 95%–97% of its correlation on Qwen 3B, which argues against a trivial positional explanation. Finally, deletion studies show that removing tokens ranked highly by the prior hurts recognition more than removing energy-matched or position-matched tokens, making the predicted score look functionally meaningful rather than merely correlated.65:T78b,The evaluation spans 13 large audio language models. On 11 of them, the linear prior predicts the all-layer attention ranking with Spearman correlation ρ ≥ 0.69. By contrast, common heuristics such as loudness, self-information, and encoder attention reach at most |ρ| = 0.31 on seven tested models. This is the central empirical result: future LM usage is much more predictable from encoder representations than from standard salience heuristics.

The paper first establishes why image-style pruning intuition does not transfer to audio. On Qwen3-Omni-30B, at layer 2, text positions allocate 16.2% of their attention to audio, versus only 3.6% to images and 3.9% to video. In a controlled comparison using the same RACE passage rendered as speech versus as a page image, audio receives 2.3× the page’s layer-2 attention on Qwen 30B and 2.1× on Qwen 3B. Meanwhile, the agreement between layer-2 ranking and final all-layer ranking is only ρ = 0.39, so early LM attention is not yet a reliable ranking signal for audio.

On transcription, under a conservative budget, Triage keeps WER within 0.04 of full-audio inference. Under an aggressive budget, it achieves lower WER than every baseline, including mid-prefill methods, in all 12 transcription settings. On multiple-choice tasks, at 2.2× to 5× compression, Triage outperforms DART—the strongest baseline on average—by 0.043 mean accuracy. The systems impact is also concrete: on Qwen2.5-Omni-3B, a 2.86× pre-LM cut increases the amount of audio that fits in context from 21.8 minutes to about 62 minutes. On natural recordings of 20–43 minutes, aggressive Triage beats truncation, one-minute window voting, and DART at matched compression. At the most compressive setting, one GPU can serve 4× as many concurrent streams.

These results matter because they show gains not only on offline accuracy metrics, but also on context capacity and serving throughput.66:T537,For a quick but useful read, focus on three parts. Two deeper questions are worth carrying forward. One is where the linear predictability comes from: does the encoder itself learn a notion of downstream semantic utility, or does the projector/LM impose a stable preferred subspace? The other is whether this signal can be pushed back into training, for example as an auxiliary objective for encoder/projector learning or as supervision for sparse audio tokenizers.67:T52e,The proposed method, Learnable Subspace Projections, assigns an orthogonal projector to each target linear layer, or to a tied group of layers that read the same activation. For a linear layer with weight W, the method learns an orthonormal matrix U and applies P=I-UU^T in the input space, thereby removing k input directions. Layers such as Q/K/V projections, or gate/up projections in the MLP, can share one projector because they consume the same activation space. During compression, pretrained weights are frozen and only the projectors are optimized. The default objective is KL divergence between the compressed model’s output distribution and the dense model’s output distribution; an alternative variant optimizes the original training objective. The method uses an activation-space parameterization and fused QR orthonormalization to keep the constrained optimization tractable at billion-parameter scale. Initialization comes from a whitened truncation rather than plain SVD. Rank allocation is also loss-aware: each candidate projector is applied in isolation, the induced output KL is measured, and the compression budget is allocated according to KL cost per saved parameter. After optimization, the projectors are merged into ordinary low-rank factors, so inference does not require LSP-specific operators.68:T4bd,DecoMoE applies structured compression along two dimensions. The Sample-Adaptive Visual Boundary predicts, for each input, the layer at which full visual-token propagation can stop. A lightweight gate reads hidden states at candidate sparse layers; if triggered, it removes the whole visual-token block before self-attention in that layer, turning subsequent computation into text-only processing. The gate is trained with supervision from forced-exit correctness and first-token negative log-likelihood while keeping the multimodal backbone frozen. The Routing-Calibrated Expert Prefix compresses expert computation. It first calibrates expert importance offline using text-token routed mass, orders experts layer by layer with a Mean-Mass criterion, and physically reorders router outputs and expert parameters so that important experts form a contiguous prefix. At inference time, each layer keeps the shortest prefix that covers a target fraction of the current activated routed mass, and native token-wise Top-k routing is restricted to that prefix. The key difference from ordinary expert pruning is that it preserves dynamic routing while making the executable expert span contiguous and hardware-friendly.69:T638,Each reasoning trajectory induces a K-dimensional probability vector θ over candidate answers. In the black-box setting, one only observes a sampled label from θ. In the grey-box setting, one observes θ itself, along with the sampled answer. The goal is sequential sampling with a stopping rule that returns the true modal answer with probability at least 1-δ at any stopping time. The theory first derives asymptotic lower bounds on expected stopping time under different observation models. A key result is that grey-box feedback is never worse than black-box feedback, and its benefit depends on the structure of the trajectory-level answer distributions. When trajectories are effectively one-hot, grey-box reduces to black-box and the complexity is of order Θ(Δ^-2). When trajectories expose stable beliefs across candidates, the complexity can improve to Θ(Δ^-1), where Δ is the frequency gap between the top answer and the runner-up. The proposed algorithm, ASC-D, is the grey-box analogue of adaptive self-consistency. Instead of counting answer labels, it accumulates pairwise evidence using probability differences θ_i-θ_j and stops when one candidate has enough certified advantage over every alternative. The design is distribution-free in the sense that it does not assume prior knowledge of the trajectory distribution, yet it provides anytime δ-correctness and asymptotically matches the lower bound. Relative to prior adaptive SC methods, the real shift is the observation model: the method operates on distribution-valued feedback rather than answer-only samples.6a:T447,The empirical section includes both synthetic and real evaluations. The synthetic experiments validate the theory: as the modal gap Δ shrinks, the advantage of grey-box feedback becomes larger, and the observed stopping-time behavior falls between the predicted Δ^-1 and Δ^-2 regimes depending on how informative the trajectory-level probability vectors are. The real benchmark is MMLU-Redux with multiple-choice questions, where the final-token probabilities over answer options can be extracted directly. Models include Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B, and Qwen3-1.7B. On these tasks, ASC-D uses 46.4% to 95.6% fewer trajectories than answer-only baselines when the modal gap is small. Under a fixed maximum budget of N=128, it also achieves the best correct-certification rate across all tested confidence levels, which matters because the gain is not merely earlier stopping but more reliable certified decisions under the same compute cap. The appendices provide additional implementation details on extracting option probabilities and extra ablations on synthetic and real settings.6b:T924,方法上有两个核心组件。第一个是 HBM–HBF–host 的分层存储系统。作者把模型权重、活跃 KV、可复用 prefix cache 分别看作不同访问模式的数据对象，在 HBM、HBF、host DRAM、SSD 之间做分层驻留和迁移。新生成的 KV 和从低层重载回来的 prefix 先进入 HBM；当 HBM 紧张时，较冷的数据再下沉到 HBF 或更低层。这里的关键不是简单 LRU，而是结合各层容量、带宽、读写代价来决定什么该放哪一层。文章还比较了两种硬件组织：shared-site 架构与 H3 架构，前者 HBM/HBF 共享有限站点，后者 HBF 链接在 HBM 之后，给系统设计提供了更具体的硬件背景。

第二个组件是 buffered cache-aware scheduling。作者观察到，如果调度器只追求尽快塞满设备，很容易把 HBM 挤满，导致后续 decode 增长或跨轮复用 prefix 时不得不频繁驱逐和回载缓存。于是他们引入 admission buffer，也就是主动保留一部分 headroom，不把内存用到极限。这个策略看起来保守，但在多轮工作负载里反而能减少 cache churn、降低 HBF 写入、提高整体完成时间。这里的思路和很多训练系统里的“不要把某个资源打满”很像：局部利用率最大化不等于全局吞吐最优。

评估方法是 request-level simulator，底层 kernel latency model 用 GPU 实测拟合。模拟器支持异步多副本执行、mixed prefill/decode batching、chunked prefill、session 内顺序依赖、多层级 cache residency 跟踪，以及 dense model 和 sparse-MoE model 的不同权重/专家放置。作者关注的指标不是单请求 latency，而是 fixed workload completion time、modeled energy、cache hit、KV writes 和基于 endurance 的寿命估计。这和他们的目标一致：研究高吞吐、可容忍较高单请求延迟的工作负载，比如 synthetic data generation、异步 agent workflow、RL rollouts。

和已有工作相比，文章的区别不在于单点优化某个 kernel，而在于把容量扩展、KV 复用、调度和写寿命放到同一个分析框架里。很多 serving 论文只讨论 HBM 内的 batching 或 prefix cache；这篇文章更关心当设备侧出现一种“比 HBM 慢、但比 host 近得多”的新层级后，系统策略如何随之改变。6c:T869,The method has two main components. The first is an HBM–HBF–host hierarchical storage system. The paper treats model weights, active KV state, and reusable prefix caches as distinct data objects with different access patterns, and manages their placement across HBM, HBF, host DRAM, and SSD. Newly generated KV state and reloaded prefixes enter HBM first; colder cache can be demoted to HBF or lower tiers when HBM becomes scarce. The point is not a simple cache policy but a placement strategy that accounts for each tier’s capacity and access cost. The paper also compares two hardware organizations—Sandisk’s shared-site architecture and the H3 architecture—so the storage policy is grounded in realistic hardware assumptions.

The second component is buffered cache-aware scheduling. The authors observe that aggressively filling device memory can be counterproductive in multi-turn workloads: it leaves no room for decode growth and forces frequent eviction of reusable prefixes, which then have to be reloaded or recomputed. Their solution is to reserve headroom through an admission buffer. This looks conservative locally, but improves global throughput by reducing cache churn, HBF writes, and repeated prefill. The idea is familiar from other large-scale systems: maximizing instantaneous utilization of one resource does not necessarily maximize end-to-end throughput.

Evaluation is done with a request-level simulator whose kernel latency models are fitted to GPU measurements. The simulator supports asynchronous execution across replicas, mixed prefill/decode batching, chunked prefill, session ordering constraints, and cache residency tracking across all tiers. It also models both dense and sparse-MoE serving, including weight and expert placement choices. The primary metrics are fixed-workload completion time, modeled energy, cache-hit fraction, KV writes, and endurance-based lifetime estimates. That metric choice matches the target setting: high-throughput workloads such as synthetic-data generation, asynchronous agent workflows, and RL rollouts, where per-request latency can be traded off for overall throughput.6d:T685,The headline results are straightforward. On 1× traces for Llama-3.1-405B and GLM-5.2, hybrid systems that keep weights in HBM reduce completion time by 46.0% to 56.3% and modeled energy by 14.4% to 24.1% relative to HBM-only baselines. This indicates that extra device-side capacity can be converted into better weight reuse and less repeated prefill rather than simply causing more movement overhead.

The scheduling experiment is also informative. Reserving 10% headroom with buffered cache-aware scheduling reduces completion time by 4.7% relative to unbuffered cache-aware scheduling, while extending estimated HBF write lifetime from 4.77 years to 14.82 years under the paper’s endurance model. That is a useful systems result: leaving some memory unused can improve both throughput and device longevity.

The paper also provides trace-driven analysis of where the gains come from in dense versus sparse-MoE serving, and how longer conversations change the trade-offs. From the provided content, the decomposition includes weight reuse, avoided repeated prefill, KV access cost, cross-tier data movement, and parallelism effects. In MoE serving, expert placement matters because not all weights are equally hot. In longer conversations, retained prefixes become more valuable, but KV pressure and write pressure also increase.

One caveat is important: these are simulator-based results with latency and energy models, not full production deployment measurements. The paper is therefore strongest as a characterization of when HBF is useful and what policies make it useful, rather than as a direct claim about guaranteed gains on a specific commercial system.6e:T51c,For a quick read, start with the introduction and methodology. Three assumptions drive the whole paper: the target is high throughput rather than low latency; the workloads are multi-turn and agentic; and HBF is constrained not only by read cost but also by slow writes and finite endurance. Once those are clear, the design choices make sense.

Then focus on the hierarchical storage policy and buffered scheduling. For the former, track which objects are prioritized in HBM and which are demoted to HBF or host tiers. For the latter, understand why admission headroom reduces eviction and reload churn. In the experiments, prioritize the plots for completion time, energy, cache hit rate, KV writes, and lifetime estimate rather than looking only at TPOT, because the optimization target is workload-level efficiency, not single-request responsiveness.

If your background is in training or RL systems rather than serving kernels, the dense-vs-MoE and short-vs-long conversation analyses are still worth reading. They help reason about the trade-off between retaining more cache and admitting more concurrent work in rollout clusters. A skim takes about 30 minutes. A more careful read of the simulator assumptions, trace construction, and hardware-architecture differences will take around 1.5 to 2 hours.6f:T894,技术上，论文先把“realization”定义清楚：同一个 fast matrix multiplication 算法，系数、量化方式、缩放策略、执行顺序不同，量化后行为会很不一样。作者分析的是两层 Strassen 在 FP8 下的 realization。已有稳定性准则通常只看系数幅值，例如误差上界参数或期望误差指标；但这些准则对 sign variants 不敏感，而 sign flip 在精确算术下不改变算法，在低精度下却会显著改变量化后的行为。作者先用这一点说明，现有准则不足以筛掉会破坏 prefix invariance 的 realization。

随后论文给出一个结构性结果：如果要求每个中间乘积在形成时就不能混入“未来行”信息，那么任何 realization 都会退化到经典乘法次数，无法保留 fast algorithm 的乘法节省。也就是说，想省乘法，就必须允许中间量跨行混合；问题不在于是否混合，而在于这种混合能否在最终输出前被无舍入地精确消掉。

基于这个观察，作者构造了 certified realization。做法不是在浮点值上直接混合，而是先对每个 token row 独立量化成整数 codes，之后 fast algorithm 的块和、块乘、抵消都在有界整数域里完成。因为整数求和不发生舍入，只要中间范围受控，跨行混合项就能被精确抵消。缩放因子则延后到整数乘加之后，再按 classical int8 operator 的方式应用。作者设计了一个 certificate，检查两件事：一是整数计算全过程不会溢出、因此保持精确；二是最终缩放与累加顺序可与 classical int8 完全对齐。凡是通过 certificate 的 realization，输出都与 classical int8 bit-for-bit 相同，因此自动继承其 row-local 性质和 prefix invariance。

论文还分析了两层 Strassen 的 512 个 sign variants。结论很强：在所提 certified scheme 下，这 512 个变体全部通过认证，且输出位级一致；而在普通 FP8 block scaling 下，它们的 teacher-forced perplexity 可以相差 772.4 倍。这说明问题不在“选一个更稳的 sign”，而在 realization 是否从构造上消除了舍入破坏抵消的可能。70:T9a7,The paper first makes the notion of a realization explicit: the same fast matrix multiplication algorithm can behave very differently after quantization depending on coefficients, scaling, quantization schedule, and execution details. The study focuses on FP8 realizations of two-level Strassen. Existing stability criteria typically depend only on coefficient magnitudes, for example through rounding-error bounds or expected-error surrogates. But sign variants of the same exact algorithm share those magnitude-based scores, even though sign flips can materially change quantized behavior. This already suggests that common criteria are too coarse for selecting realizations that preserve causal semantics.

The authors then prove a structural limitation. If one insists that every intermediate product feeding an output row must itself avoid dependence on later rows, then one is forced back to the classical multiplication count. In other words, any realization that keeps the fast multiplication savings must allow intermediate cross-row mixing. The real question is whether that mixing is undone exactly before the final output is formed.

Their certified construction answers yes by moving the cancellation into bounded integer arithmetic. Each token row is quantized independently into integer codes. The fast algorithm then mixes, multiplies, and cancels these integer codes rather than floating-point values. Since integer sums do not round, cross-row terms can cancel exactly as long as intermediate ranges remain bounded. Scaling factors are applied only afterward, aligned with the classical int8 operator. The certificate checks two things: that the integer computation remains exact throughout, and that the final scaling and accumulation can be matched to classical int8 in the same order. Any realization that passes the certificate is bit-for-bit identical to the classical int8 operator with the same codes and scales. Because the classical int8 operator is row-local, certified realizations inherit prefix invariance automatically.

A notable result concerns the 512 sign variants of two-level Strassen. Under ordinary FP8 block scaling, these variants can behave wildly differently after quantization. Under the certified int8 construction, all 512 pass the certificate and produce identical output bits. This shows that the key issue is not selecting a numerically lucky sign pattern, but eliminating rounding-sensitive cancellation by construction.71:T6cc,The empirical section has two main parts. The first demonstrates the failure mode. On Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct evaluated on OpenBookQA, two repaired FP8 fast realizations achieve 35.42% and 32.92% accuracy, compared with 34.58% for the bf16 model. By ordinary accuracy, one might conclude the first realization is fine. The paper then introduces a prefix-invariance test: keep the allowed prefix fixed, replace only the text after that prefix with the bf16 model’s own greedy continuation, and rescore the original answer by likelihood. Under this test, the two FP8 realizations change the selected answer on 5.83% and 10.00% of 240 items, respectively. The bf16 baseline and a deployed row-local FP8 kernel change none. Since the allowed prefix, shapes, and execution plan are unchanged, these answer flips directly expose dependence on forbidden future text.

The second part studies stability criteria and certification. For the 512 sign variants of two-level Strassen under the same FP8 schedule with block scaling, teacher-forced perplexity spans a 772.4x range, while the analyzed coefficient-magnitude criteria assign them identical scores. This is strong evidence that those criteria do not resolve the quantized behaviors that matter in practice. For the certified realizations, all 512 sign variants pass the certificate and match classical int8 bit for bit, while reducing the number of block multiplications from 64 to 49 for the 4x4 partition. The paper also reports initial timing results, with an important caveat: fewer block multiplications do not automatically translate into faster end-to-end kernels. The current implementation establishes correctness and feasibility; kernel-level speedups remain future engineering work.72:T491,For a quick read, focus on three parts. If time is limited, a 30–45 minute pass through problem setup, counterexample experiments, certified construction, and timing discussion is enough to capture the main contribution. For each trace, it samples candidate prefix boundaries at paragraph breaks, sentence endings, and positions before reflection phrases such as “Wait” or “Alternatively”, with at most 40 boundaries per trace. For each prefix, it appends a closing tag and a final-answer prompt, then greedily decodes a short answer of up to 16 tokens. The terminal reasoning prefix is read out in the same way. A boundary is labeled stable if every later readout is mathematically equivalent to the terminal readout. If any later readout changes, the boundary remains a continue target, even when the current answer happens to be correct. Equivalence is checked by normalized string comparison followed by Math-Verify symbolic checking.

Training directly supervises the probability of the existing </think> token at labeled boundaries. Stable boundaries receive stop targets; earlier boundaries receive continue targets. Other response positions are regularized with a KL penalty toward the frozen base model distribution. Boundary positions are excluded from the KL term. This differs from full-sequence SFT: SFT learns both a particular shortened reasoning continuation and a stopping point, while Settle only trains the stopping decision and treats all positions in the stable suffix as valid opportunities to stop. At inference time, </think> simply competes with other vocabulary tokens under ordinary decoding.74:T4ad,The study uses three settings. E1 measures spontaneous reward hacking: 17 language models each receive one full sandboxed terminal-agent attempt on each of 38 tasks, without being instructed or authorized to hack. An attempt is a complete ReAct-style agent session, not a single model response. The agent can inspect files, call tools, run the visible scorer, edit its solution, and resubmit until a 40-turn or 3600-second limit. The reported evidence suggests that overall model rankings are more stable than individual answers and domain-level profiles.77:T457,The method uses a closed-testing construction. An independent proposal split nominates one candidate-specific floor c_k for each policy. A fresh certification split then runs an exact binomial test for H_k: P(S_k < c_k) ≥ α. Rejecting this null certifies that the candidate’s lower α-quantile is at least the proposed floor. Holm’s step-down procedure controls the family-wise error rate at δ across candidates. The selected policy is the certified candidate with the largest floor; the procedure abstains if no certified floor exceeds a predeclared operating threshold. The guarantee allows arbitrary within-unit dependence across candidates, such as correlated judge scores on the same prompt, while requiring i.i.d. evaluation units. Compared with matched-proposal Bonferroni, Holm gives a uniformly stronger rejection set on every dataset. Compared with exact COPS, it certifies a different statistical object, so uniform dominance is not claimed. The score map s_k is treated as a fixed measurable function; it need not be unbiased, Gaussian, asymptotically normal, or a mean off-policy estimator.78:T48b,The study attempted 10 open model variants across five families and a scale range from 8B to 675B parameters. Eight met the inclusion threshold: gemma3:12b, gpt-oss:20b, gpt-oss:120b, ministral-3:8b, mistral-large-3:675b, minimax-m2.1, minimax-m2.7, and qwen3-coder-next. deepseek-v3.1:671b produced no successful logged inference, likely due to client timeout, but the model was retired before the cause could be established. glm-4.7 had five successful runs across two prompts and was excluded only because it fell below the three-prompt threshold. Under bootstrap, only the bottom of the ranking remains firm; the full ordered table does not.79:T84a,方法由三部分组成。第一部分是 PB-CSTE 环境。它是一个刻意简化、确定性的 stateful tool-use 环境，任务通过 allowlisted 的 create/update/delete/restore/goal-revision 操作修改带类型的实体。环境记录时间戳、actor class、state diff 和 snapshot，便于可执行回放与归因审计。作者主动去掉网络、并发、权限系统、随机失败和开放式浏览，这样做不是为了贴近真实世界，而是为了把“评测器是否被历史状态欺骗”这个因果问题单独拎出来。

第二部分是双向量认证。对每条轨迹，私有 certifier 构造两个向量：一个是最终时刻哪些 goal predicates 为真，对应 current-state progress；另一个是这些已满足谓词里，哪些应按事件日志规则归因给 agent，对应 agent-attributed progress。pair eligibility 要求 honest 轨迹 H 和 adversarial 轨迹 A 在这两个向量上逐项相等。这样控制住了两件事：终态真实进展相同，且可归因给 agent 的进展也相同。论文把这称为 certified equal-progress。这里的归因不是一般因果归因，而是 benchmark 内部标准化的事件日志归因规则，目的是让比较可执行、可审计。

第三部分是两类 stress protocol。其一是 equal-progress pair：在相同认证进展下，若 evaluator 给 A 更高分，则说明 evaluator 奖励了历史峰值、状态 churn、重建实体或归因歧义。其二是 strict rollback：从 honest 轨迹出发，执行一个合法逆操作，要求 active goal 不变且 current-state progress 严格下降。如果 evaluator 对 rollback 不敏感，就说明它对真实进展损失不够敏感。

理论上，作者给了两个命题。命题1说明，任何只依赖最终认证状态与认证归因的 evaluator，在 matched pair 上都应满足零膨胀。命题2说明，任何取历史最大值的 evaluator，都可能在终态相同的情况下被 adversarial witness 拉高分数。这个形式化很朴素，但足够把“current-state evaluator”和“historical evaluator”的差别说清楚。7a:T7e5,实验在 PB-CSTE v1.0 上做，包含 6 个开发任务和 18 个 sealed held-out 任务，任务类型覆盖 persistent multi-step、CRUD、fixed-goal interaction 和 GoalPatch。每个任务有 3 到 5 个持久 goal predicates，honest progress 覆盖从 1/4 到 3/4 的七个层级。最终在 18 个 held-out 任务中，历史目标运行成功构造出 15 个 canonical equal-progress adversaries。

核心结果有三组。第一组是历史式评分器的脆弱性。historical scoring 的平均 inflation 为 0.252，条件攻击成功数为 10/15，端到端 yield 为 10/18；在 rollback 检测上是 0/14，几乎完全失效。这说明只要评分器把历史上达到过的里程碑也算分，就很容易被合法 witness 利用。

第二组是语义 judge 的迁移表现。一个 structured DeepSeek judge 把 transfer inflation 降到 0.022，并能检测 10/14 个 rollback，明显比纯历史式规则好，但仍非零，说明语义 judge 即使更强，也会被定向构造的 witness 诱导。Independent-Decomposition Judge（IDJ）从任务说明中构造冻结 checklist，不访问 Oracle schema，得到 mean transfer inflation 0.017、ASR 1/15、rollback detection 12/14。这个结果说明，只要 checklist 真正锚定终态分解，而不是追踪历史痕迹，哪怕不直接访问私有 schema，也能接近 current-state 规则。

第三组是正控制。current-state rules 在该环境里达到零 inflation，并检测全部 rollback。论文解释得很清楚：PB-CSTE 中公开的 CSPS 组件与私有 certified state 一一对应，Lightweight CAPE 还额外用对应 attribution 组件，因此它们是结构性正控制，不是开放世界下的通用解法。

值得注意的实验细节是，作者还做了 replay audit，确认 15 个 canonical pair 的状态向量和归因向量确实完全匹配；并区分了 witness construction、inflation、coverage、transfer 和 rollback sensitivity 这些不同维度，而不是只报一个攻击成功率。7b:T869,The method has three layers. First, the authors build PB-CSTE, a deterministic stateful tool-use environment designed for causal isolation. Tasks operate over typed entities through allowlisted create, update, delete, restore, and goal-revision actions. Every successful operation logs timestamps, actor class, state diffs, and snapshots. The environment intentionally excludes networking, concurrency, permissions, stochastic failures, and open-ended browsing. That simplification is deliberate: the goal is to isolate evaluator failure modes, not to mimic the full messiness of real-world agents.

Second, they define dual-vector certification. For each trusted terminal state, a private certifier constructs a state vector indicating which goal predicates hold at termination, and an attribution vector indicating which satisfied predicates receive standardized agent credit under an event-log rule. A pair is eligible only if the honest trajectory H and adversarial trajectory A match component-wise on both vectors. This controls both final retained progress and credited progress. The attribution rule is not presented as general causal attribution; it is a benchmark-internal standardization that makes the comparison executable and auditable.

Third, they introduce two stress protocols. Equal-progress pairs test invariance: if an evaluator gives A a higher score than H despite identical certified progress, the extra score must come from historical peaks, churn, recreated entities, or attribution ambiguity. Strict rollback tests sensitivity: starting from H, apply a legal inverse transition that lowers certified current-state progress while keeping the active goal fixed. If the evaluator fails to penalize rollback, it is not tracking actual progress loss.

The formal section is simple but useful. Proposition 1 shows that any evaluator depending only on certified final state and certified attribution must have zero inflation on matched pairs. Proposition 2 shows that historical-max evaluators can be exploited whenever the adversarial trajectory reaches a higher intermediate peak, even if the final certified vectors are identical.7c:T813,Experiments use PB-CSTE v1.0 with 6 development tasks and 18 sealed held-out tasks, spanning persistent multi-step tasks, CRUD tasks, fixed-goal interactions, and GoalPatch cases. Each task has 3 to 5 persistent goal predicates, and honest prefixes cover seven progress levels from 1/4 to 3/4. On the 18 held-out tasks, the historical-target procedure successfully constructs 15 canonical equal-progress adversaries.

The main result is the weakness of historical scoring. Historical scoring shows mean inflation of 0.252, conditional attack success on 10/15 matched pairs, end-to-end yield of 10/18, and rollback detection of 0/14. In other words, once the evaluator rewards historical milestones, legal witnesses can often inflate the score without increasing certified final progress.

The second result concerns semantic judges. A structured DeepSeek judge reduces transfer inflation to 0.022 and detects 10/14 rollbacks. That is much better than purely historical rules, but still not zero. An Independent-Decomposition Judge (IDJ), which builds frozen checklists from task instructions without access to the private Oracle schema, achieves mean transfer inflation of 0.017, attack success 1/15, and rollback detection 12/14. This is an important finding: a judge can get close to current-state behavior if its checklist is anchored to final-state decomposition rather than historical traces, even without direct access to the certifier schema.

The positive controls are current-state rules. In PB-CSTE they achieve zero inflation and detect all rollbacks. The paper is careful here: these are structural positive controls because public CSPS components map one-to-one to the private certified state components in this benchmark. That does not mean the same solution transfers unchanged to open-world agent evaluation.

Existing benchmark scores provide unstable diagnostics: upstream capability scores do not reliably predict hallucination, and even benchmarks assigned to the same stage can move in opposite directions. The causal interventions are clearer. Each task pins one match target before any agent run: the cheapest reported configuration that still supports the paper’s central empirical claim, together with the metric, reported value, evaluation scope, and success tolerance. Tasks are stratified by released artifacts. Run-tier papers provide code, data, and weights. Retrain-tier papers lack weights, so the agent must train the model. Reimplement-tier papers lack code, so the agent must implement the method from the paper. The benchmark does not provide scripted pipelines or prepared environments. Agents must plan the reproduction, install software, resolve dependency failures, manage GPU allocations, and produce execution evidence. Scoring is based on logs and outputs rather than the agent’s own narrative, using a separate language-model grader to audit whether the run supports the pinned claim. Muse Spark 1.2 reaches 15% on Reimplement-tier, the best result for that tier. A notable finding is that Run-tier remains difficult despite providing all major artifacts.
