The provided text does not include full tables, model sizes, dataset sizes, or exact improvement numbers, so those should not be invented. When reading the original, the most useful experimental artifacts to extract are the stability-boundary plots, the comparisons against vanilla GD, and any quantitative alignment between the theorem and observed training dynamics.18a:T58c,Read it in the order of phenomenon, model, theorem, then proof technique.

Start with the introduction and lock onto the practical question: why can a long high-LR phase plus sharp decay outperform smoother schedules, and what role does momentum play there? Then jump to Theorem 4.1. That is the central statement of the paper: the maximum stable learning rate is enlarged by about (1+β)/(1-β).

After that, spend time on Lemma 5.1 and the surrounding proof structure. This is where the real novelty sits. The important part is not only the final factor, but how the authors control dynamics when the river and valley subspaces rotate and when gradient and momentum components interfere with each other. While reading, focus on three things: how the river/valley projections are defined and updated, what assumptions encode “flat” and “slow-spinning,” and how the error terms are prevented from accumulating into instability.

If time is limited, read the theorem statements, proof sketches, and the main figures first, then return to the technical induction details. Also check the remark on the improved vanilla-GD learning-rate bound; it helps assess whether the analytical framework has broader value beyond the momentum case.

A careful read will likely take 1.5 to 2.5 hours. For readers focused on training stability and optimizer dynamics, this is worth reading with equations and figures side by side.18b:T7f3,技术上分三层。第一层是机制定位。作者从 softmax backward 的标准形式 dS = P ⊙ (dP - δ) 出发，其中每一行的 δ_i = Σ_j P_ij dP_ij，本来保证 dS 每行求和为 0，这对应 softmax 对行平移不变。FP8 attention 的常见实现为了省算，会用保存下来的输出 O 来近似这个 row correction，即 δ_i^stale = <dO_i, Ô_i>。在高精度或前后向操作数一致时，这个捷径成立；但在 FP8 下，forward 用的是量化后的 P、V 得到 Ô，backward 又用重新量化后的 dO、V 得到 dP̂，两边的量化误差来源不同，导致 δ_i^stale 不再等于真正与 dP̂ 匹配的 correction。

第二层是误差如何影响训练。作者推导出 stale delta 会让 dS 的每一行出现非零残差 ε_i = Σ_j dS_ij^stale。这个残差不是无害的，因为它等价于在 matched gradient 上额外加了 ε_i P_ij 这一项。若 ε_i<0，会推动该行 logits 变尖；若 ε_i>0，会推动其变平。表面上看，不同行的残差可能互相抵消，但映射到 channel 维度后并不会自然抵消。作者观察到某些被“偏爱”的通道会持续受到同向压力，尤其体现在 key 侧 RMSNorm gain 被系统性推高，随后形成选择性放大，训练越久越明显。

第三层是修复方法 Delta-Matching。核心思想不是简单提高某个张量精度，而是让 backward row correction 使用与 backward 真实乘法路径一致的量。作者从未量化的 softmax 概率 P 和由 FP8 backward operands 在 FP32 中相乘得到的 dP̂ 出发，重新构造匹配的 δ，使 softmax gradient 的零行和不变量在给定数值假设下恢复。文中还特别说明，只把 dO 保留成 BF16 并不够，因为概率量化带来的不一致仍在。Delta-Matching 的价值在于它不依赖额外保存一个高精度 forward output，也不要求改 attention 结构；它针对的是 backward correction 这个具体失配点，因此可以直接嵌入 native block-scaled FP8 attention kernel。18c:T822,实验设计比较扎实，重点不只是“最终分数更高”，而是把失效边界画出来了。首先在机制验证上，作者拿 1.67B GDN/GQA 训练末期 checkpoint 的 BF16 重算激活，去探测 FP8 kernel 在 6 个 attention layer、32 个训练窗口上的行为。结果显示，在 dS 量化之前，stale delta 造成的归一化 row-sum residual 中位数大约在 1.1e-2 到 4.7e-2，这已经不是可忽略的舍入噪声量级。

规模实验覆盖 569M、1.67B、5.29B。569M 上，stale-delta hybrid 只表现为较温和的 validation loss gap，下游任务大体还能保住；这解释了为什么一些早期工作在 sub-billion 规模上看起来“FP8 attention 也能训”。但到 1.67B 和 5.29B，训练前期还能跟住 BF16/FP32 mixed-precision reference，之后 loss 开始持续抬升，并带来下游性能下降，而且 5.29B 更早出现拐点，符合“误差积累且随规模加速”的判断。

作者还测试了多种可能的缓解手段。QK normalization 能减轻甚至避免某些配置下的灾难性崩溃，但仍留有明显性能差距；NoPE 在保留位置敏感 recurrent 层时只能延后退化；head dimension 从 128 提到 256 没有根治作用。这些结果说明问题不是某个架构细节偶然触发，而是 attention backward 数值约束被破坏后的普遍现象。

在架构泛化上，作者不只测标准 attention，还测了 Gated DeltaNet + MLA 的 hybrid，以及 KDA + GQA 的组合，stale-delta failure 都存在。在线性层精度、模型结构、训练阶段变化下，Delta-Matching 都能把训练 loss 和整体下游表现拉回到 BF16/FP32 mixed-precision attention reference 附近。

长上下文实验也很关键。按 Kimi K2 / DeepSeek-V3 风格 recipe，从 8K 扩到 64K，并把学习率降下来后，stale-delta baseline 相对 BF16/FP32 的 training-loss gap 要到大约 19k optimizer steps、约 20B tokens 后才超过 0.01。这个结果很有信息量：如果只做短程 context extension 验证，很容易误判为“方法没问题”。18d:T7df,The technical story has three parts. First, the paper localizes the failure. Softmax backward has the form dS = P ⊙ (dP - δ), where δ_i = Σ_j P_ij dP_ij for each row. In exact arithmetic this guarantees that each row of dS sums to zero, reflecting softmax shift invariance. Many efficient implementations reuse the saved forward output O to compute the row correction, using δ_i^stale = <dO_i, O_hat_i>. This shortcut is valid when the forward and backward quantities are numerically consistent. Under FP8, however, O_hat comes from quantized forward operands, while dP_hat is formed from separately quantized backward operands. The two paths no longer match, so the shortcut becomes stale.

Second, the paper analyzes how this mismatch affects optimization. The stale correction induces a nonzero row residual ε_i = Σ_j dS_ij^stale. That residual adds an extra term ε_i P_ij to the matched gradient. Negative ε_i sharpens a row of logits; positive ε_i flattens it. Even if row-wise residuals nearly cancel globally, they do not cancel channel-wise after projection through Q/K/V. The authors show persistent pressure on selected channels, especially visible as systematic upward drift in key-side RMSNorm gains. This creates selective amplification over training rather than zero-mean noise.

Third, the proposed fix is Delta-Matching. The key idea is to compute the backward row correction from quantities that are actually consistent with the backward path: unquantized softmax probabilities P and FP32 products formed from the FP8 backward operands. Under the stated numerical assumptions, this restores the zero-row-sum invariant. The paper also shows that simply keeping dO in BF16 is insufficient, because the mismatch caused by probability quantization remains. Delta-Matching is attractive because it does not require storing an auxiliary high-precision forward output and does not depend on architectural changes. It directly patches the numerical inconsistency at the backward correction step.18e:T81e,The experiments are strong because they map out the failure regime instead of only reporting end metrics. For mechanism validation, the authors probe the FP8 kernel using BF16-recomputed activations from final 1.67B GDN/GQA checkpoints, across six attention layers and 32 training windows. Before dS quantization, stale delta produces normalized row-sum residuals around 1.1e-2 to 4.7e-2 on average row medians over nonzero-gradient rows. That is far above negligible rounding noise.

The scale study covers 569M, 1.67B, and 5.29B models. At 569M, stale-delta hybrid training shows only a modest validation-loss gap and largely preserves downstream quality. This helps explain why earlier small-scale studies could appear encouraging. At 1.67B and 5.29B, however, stale-delta runs initially track BF16/FP32 references, then diverge later with rising loss and degraded downstream performance. The onset is earlier at 5.29B, consistent with cumulative error that accelerates with scale.

The paper also tests several mitigations. QK normalization can prevent catastrophic collapse in some settings, but it still leaves a substantial performance gap. NoPE delays degradation but does not remove it. Increasing head dimension from 128 to 256 does not solve the problem either. This is useful because it shows the issue is not an artifact of one architecture choice.

Generality is tested beyond a single attention design. The stale-delta failure appears in hybrids combining Gated DeltaNet with MLA, and KDA with GQA. Across architectures, training stages, and linear-layer precision settings, Delta-Matching recovers training loss and overall downstream performance close to BF16/FP32 mixed-precision attention references.

The long-context extension result is especially informative. Using a Kimi K2 / DeepSeek-V3 style recipe to extend from 8K to 64K with a lower learning rate, the stale-delta baseline does not exceed a 0.01 training-loss gap over BF16/FP32 until roughly 19k optimizer steps, about 20B tokens. This shows why short extension runs can miss the problem entirely.18f:T559,Start with Sections 3.2 to 3.4. The main thing to understand is why the zero-row-sum property is not a cosmetic identity but the backward expression of softmax shift invariance, and why the saved-output shortcut breaks under FP8. Then read Figure 3 carefully. It is the bridge from local numerical inconsistency to long-horizon optimization damage, especially the channel-selective amplification story. After that, go to the scale and context-extension experiments in Section 4, focusing on the contrast between 569M, 1.67B, and 5.29B, and on the delayed failure during 8K to 64K extension.

Two details are worth extra attention. First, the paper shows that matching output-gradient precision alone is not enough. That is a broader lesson for low-precision training: local precision patches often fail if forward and backward are still inconsistent at the algorithmic level. Second, the mitigation results for QK norm and NoPE are useful because they separate error sensitivity from error source. They make training less fragile, but they do not repair the broken invariant.

For a fast read, spend most time on the derivation of stale delta, Figure 3, and the 1.67B main pretraining results. For implementation or reproduction, the appendices matter because the numerical assumptions and residual definitions are important to interpret the proof and the measurements.190:T8e9,实验部分信息量比较足，且不只停留在 ImageNet 分类。

1. 视觉监督训练：作者用约 1M 参数的 core 去初始化 85M 参数的 ViT-Base，再在 ImageNet-1K 上训练，top-1 相比随机初始化提升 +2.2 个百分点。这是最核心的 headline result，因为它说明一个很小的 recurrent core 可以迁移到大得多的目标模型，并带来稳定收益。

2. 下游表征质量：论文没有把收益局限在分类，而是检查了更能反映表征结构的任务。给出的数字包括：ADE20K 语义分割 mIoU 从 26.6 提升到 28.8；ImageNet-S 零样本分割 mAP 从 32.3 到 42.9；VOC07 目标定位 CorLoc 从 9.9 到 18.4；NYUv2 深度估计 RMSE 从 1.104 降到 0.998。这里的模式很重要：定位、分割、深度都变好，说明初始化影响的不只是分类头适配，而是中间表征更规整。

3. 自监督与跨域：作者还报告 DINO 自监督训练也有收益，说明 Procedural Core 不依赖监督标签。更关键的是，收益延伸到语言模型，在 FineWeb-Edu 自然语言数据和 CodeParrot 代码数据上训练的模型也优于随机或结构化初始化。当前片段没有给出语言实验的具体 loss 或 perplexity 数字，但这一点使它和一般 CV 初始化工作拉开了距离。

4. 对比基线：文中明确说优于 random initialization 和 structured initialization（如 Trockman and Kolter, 2023）。这说明收益不是“任何非随机初始化都行”，而是 procedural recurrent core 这个特定先验更有效。

5. 机制分析：作者发现 recurrence 带来的参数共享会把计算分布到更广的方向集合，尤其包含低能量成分；在 ViT 中，结构主要集中在 attention value/output pathway，并能抑制高范数 token outlier。这个分析很关键，因为初始化论文常见问题是“有效但说不清为什么”，而这里至少给出了一条可检验的机制链路。

如果回到预训练视角，最值得核对的细节是：语言模型实验的规模、token 数、训练步数、与 procedural warm-up 本身相比的差距有多大，以及收益是否主要体现在早期收敛还是最终 loss 也持续更优。当前片段没有完整表格，这些数字需要看原文。191:T7c0,The method is called Procedural Core. It has two stages.

Stage one trains a very small recurrent auxiliary transformer on procedural data instead of warming up each target model directly. The auxiliary model is a minimal recurrent ViT with only three unique blocks: an input block, a recurrent middle block, and an output block. The objective and procedural data setup follow prior procedural warm-up work. The key idea is not to maximize the auxiliary model’s standalone performance, but to force useful computation into a compact reusable parameter set through depth-wise sharing. Recurrence acts as a compression mechanism: if deep transformers partly implement block-recurrent programs, then a recurrent model is a natural place to store that structure compactly.

Stage two expands this compact core into a target transformer of arbitrary width and depth. Depth is handled by unrolling the recurrent block across layers. Width is handled by tiling or expansion rules that map the smaller learned weights into a wider model. The result is a deterministic initialization procedure, not a new warm-up run for each target architecture.

The novelty has three layers. First, it turns procedural pretraining from a repeated training stage into a reusable initialization asset. Second, it uses recurrence as the transfer format, rather than directly interpolating or transplanting warm-up weights. Third, the paper goes beyond reporting gains and studies why the method transfers: depth-wise sharing appears to spread computation across a broader set of directions, including lower-energy components that matter for transfer; in ViTs, the strongest effects concentrate in the attention value/output pathway and suppress high-norm token outliers.

From an LLM perspective, the most interesting part is that the same idea is tested not only in vision but also in natural language and code modeling, which argues for a more general transformer prior rather than a vision-specific trick.192:T894,The experimental section is substantial and goes well beyond ImageNet classification.

1. Supervised vision training: a roughly 1M-parameter core is expanded to initialize an 85M-parameter ViT-Base, then trained on ImageNet-1K. This gives a +2.2 point top-1 improvement over random initialization. This is the central result because it shows that a very small recurrent core can transfer to a much larger target model.

2. Representation-sensitive downstream tasks: the gains are not limited to classification. Reported numbers include ADE20K semantic segmentation improving from 26.6 to 28.8 mIoU, ImageNet-S zero-shot segmentation from 32.3 to 42.9 mAP, VOC07 localization from 9.9 to 18.4 CorLoc, and NYUv2 depth estimation improving from 1.104 to 0.998 RMSE. This pattern matters: segmentation, localization, and depth all improve, which suggests the initialization changes internal representations rather than only helping classifier fitting.

3. Self-supervised and cross-domain transfer: the paper also reports gains for DINO, so the effect is not tied to supervised labels. More importantly, the method also helps language models trained on FineWeb-Edu and code models trained on CodeParrot. The excerpt does not expose exact language-model loss or perplexity numbers, but this is what separates the work from a standard CV initialization paper.

4. Baselines: Procedural Core beats both random initialization and structured initialization baselines such as Trockman and Kolter (2023). So the result is not just “any non-random start helps.”

5. Mechanistic analysis: the paper argues that recurrence spreads useful computation across a wider set of directions, especially lower-energy ones, and that in ViTs the effect concentrates in the attention value/output pathway while suppressing high-norm token outliers. This is important because initialization papers often stop at empirical gains; here there is at least a plausible mechanism to inspect.

For pretraining readers, the main missing details to verify in the full paper are the language-model scales, token budgets, training lengths, and how close this gets to running a full procedural warm-up directly on the target model.193:T60e,This deserves more than a quick skim if you care about initialization, data efficiency, procedural data, or the idea that pretraining effects might be compressible into a parameter prior. Start with the introduction and make the distinction from prior procedural warm-up work precise: the goal is not another warm-up stage, but a reusable core that captures its benefit.

Then read the method section carefully, especially the figure and the part describing the three unique blocks, recurrent training, and the expansion rules in depth and width. The key conceptual question is why recurrence should be a better carrier of transferable structure than simply training a small feed-forward transformer.

In the experiments, first read the ImageNet result, then the segmentation/localization/depth evaluations, because those are stronger evidence that the initialization changes representation quality. After that, check the language and code experiments to judge whether the method is truly transformer-general. Finally, read the mechanistic analysis around low-energy directions, the attention value/output pathway, and token-outlier suppression. That section is not the final word, but it gives concrete handles for follow-up work.

A focused read will take around 45 minutes. The most useful follow-up questions are: how the gains scale with model size, how much is lost relative to running a full procedural warm-up on the target model, and whether this initialization interacts with tokenizer choice, data curriculum, or training cooldown recipes.194:T981,技术核心是把当前层的 full weight gradient 分解成 LoRA 可访问部分和不可访问部分。对注入 LoRA 的线性层，设有效权重为 W_base + sBA。给定当前 batch 的输入激活 X 和反向信号 δ，完整权重梯度可恢复为 G_raw = δ^T X（按文中记号，batch 和 token 维展平后计算）。作者证明，由当前 A、B 的欧氏梯度所诱导出来的等价权重空间梯度，恰好张成当前 LoRA 参数化的 tangent space，也就是所谓 LoRA-accessible gradient space。于是可以把 G_raw 正交分解为切空间内的分量和法向分量；后者被称为 normal gradient。

这个 normal gradient 有两个关键性质。第一，只要它非零，取其负方向，在固定当前 adapter 与其他权重的局部条件下，是当前 batch loss 的下降方向。第二，它与当前 LoRA 一阶可达的所有方向都正交，因此不是通过改 adapter 学习率、初始化或梯度重标定就能补回来的。这也是作者为什么不继续做 LoRA factor 的优化修补，而是直接把 normal 分量用于更新 base weights。

GDLoRA 的实现分成两条支路：adapter branch 仍然是标准 LoRA + AdamW；normal branch 则从同一次前向/反向中恢复 full gradient，投影到当前切空间的正交补上，得到 normal gradient，然后直接更新 base weights。这里有两个实现细节值得注意。其一，作者只对 normal branch 做 token-count normalization，即按输入位置数归一化梯度幅值，保持方向不变，目的是让不同序列长度或 token 数下的 normal update 更稳定。其二，base weights 不维护额外的 momentum / variance buffer，也就是不用 Adam 状态去追踪这条支路，从而避免像 FFT 那样为全量参数付出 optimizer-state 内存。这样做的取舍很明确：用更“轻”的 base update 换取部分 full-gradient 信息，而不是完全复制 FFT 的优化器行为。

和已有方法相比，差异也很清楚。Fira 试图用低秩投影近似 full-rank adaptive update，但需要周期性 SVD 或复用投影基，存在梯度子空间漂移问题。LoRA-GA、LoRA-Pro 则仍停留在 adapter 参数化内部，改善的是 LoRA 所诱导的权重梯度与 full gradient 的对齐程度。GDLoRA 直接承认当前 LoRA 切空间之外还有信息，并显式抽取这部分正交分量来更新 base weights，因此方法逻辑更直接。195:T95c,The method starts from a LoRA-injected linear layer with effective weight W_base + sBA. Given forward activations X and backward signals delta for the current batch, the unconstrained full weight gradient can be reconstructed as G_raw = delta^T X after flattening batch and token dimensions. The key theoretical result is that the set of equivalent weight-space gradients induced by Euclidean gradients on A and B coincides exactly with the tangent space of the current LoRA parameterization. This defines the LoRA-accessible gradient space.

Once this space is characterized, the full gradient can be orthogonally decomposed into a tangent component and a normal component. The latter is called the normal gradient. This component has two important properties. First, when nonzero, its negative is a local descent direction for the current batch loss when the current adapters and other parameters are held fixed. Second, it is orthogonal to every first-order direction available through the current LoRA factors, so it cannot be recovered merely by better initialization, rescaling, or re-optimizing the adapter gradients within the same parameterization.

GDLoRA uses two update branches. The adapter branch is standard LoRA optimized with AdamW. The normal branch reconstructs the full gradient from the same forward/backward pass, projects out the tangent-space component, and directly applies the remaining normal gradient to the base weights. A notable design choice is that token-count normalization is applied only to the normal branch, to stabilize update magnitude across different numbers of input positions while preserving direction. Another important choice is that the base weights do not maintain additional momentum or variance buffers. This is how the method avoids the optimizer-state overhead of FFT. In effect, GDLoRA supplements LoRA with a lightweight base-weight update that carries information unavailable to the current low-rank factors.

Compared with prior work, the distinction is clear. Fira approximates full-rank adaptive updates through projected gradients and periodically refreshed low-rank bases, which introduces basis-refresh trade-offs. LoRA-GA and LoRA-Pro improve how adapter gradients approximate the full gradient, but still remain inside the LoRA-induced update space. GDLoRA instead explicitly extracts the orthogonal complement and uses it directly.196:T5a4,The experiments span natural language understanding, mathematical and commonsense reasoning, and image classification. The main empirical claim is that under matched adapter and optimizer configurations, GDLoRA improves average performance by about 2% to 4% over standard LoRA and often approaches, or in some settings matches, full fine-tuning.

The emphasis on matched configurations matters. The paper is not claiming gains from extra trainable parameters or full optimizer states. It is testing whether the normal-gradient branch consistently adds useful information beyond what LoRA can express at first order. The most informative comparisons are therefore against standard LoRA, FFT, and methods such as Fira, LoRA-GA, and LoRA-Pro.

The ablations to pay attention to are the ones that isolate the mechanism: whether token-count normalization is necessary for the normal branch; how much is gained by combining LoRA updates with normal base-weight updates versus using either alone; how the method behaves at different ranks; and whether the benefit shrinks as rank increases. If the paper’s interpretation is correct, the gain should be more pronounced at lower ranks, where the LoRA tangent space is narrower and the normal component is more likely to contain important descent directions.

This is not a large-scale scaling-law paper. The value lies in making the missing-gradient story concrete, measurable, and empirically useful.197:T4e1,Read this paper with one question in mind: is LoRA limited mainly by low-rank capacity, or by the restricted first-order update space of its current parameterization? Start with the introduction and the theorem-level characterization that the accessible gradient space equals the tangent space. That is the conceptual center of the paper. Then read the definition and properties of the normal gradient carefully, especially why it is a local descent direction and why it cannot be represented by first-order perturbations of the current LoRA factors.

After that, inspect the algorithm section to see that GDLoRA reuses signals already available from a standard backward pass rather than introducing an expensive second-order or repeatedly decomposed procedure. In the experiments, focus on the main comparison tables against LoRA and FFT, then the comparisons with Fira, LoRA-GA, and LoRA-Pro, and finally the ablations on token normalization, rank, and base-weight update design.

A 30-minute read is enough to capture the main idea. If you want to judge whether it is practical for large-model training, spend extra time on the appendix details about compute overhead, memory accounting, and how full-gradient recovery is implemented in practice.198:T43d,The analysis is built around preconditioned SGD with a fixed positive-definite preconditioner, which makes the theory broad enough to cover simplified versions of SGD, AdaGrad, RMSProp, and Adam-like methods. For the early phase, the paper uses Lyapunov stability analysis to connect stable step size with local sharpness. Since early pre-training lies in a highly sharp region, a large learning rate before sufficient warmup violates the stability condition. This explains why warmup is not just a smoothing heuristic but a way to wait until the landscape becomes less sharp. For the late phase, the loss is locally approximated by a quadratic around a minimum, and the stochastic dynamics are analyzed under gradient noise. The resulting depth-flatness trade-off says that lower noise emphasizes loss minimization and produces deeper minima, while higher noise regularizes sharpness and pushes toward wider basins. Because the theory identifies η/B as the relevant noise-scale term, increasing batch size and decaying learning rate become two related ways of reducing stochasticity.199:T437,The main experiments use LLaMA-2 style models with 93M and 170M parameters, trained on FineWeb-Edu with context length 1024. Training budgets range from 50 to 1000 tokens per parameter. The optimizer is AdamW with β1=0.95, β2=0.95, weight decay 0.1, and gradient clipping at 1.0. Evaluation uses a held-out validation split of about 50M tokens. The empirical results support three claims. First, local sharpness is very high at the start of pre-training and then drops, matching the sharp-to-flat picture. Large peak learning rates without enough warmup lead to loss spikes or plateaus. Second, larger peak learning rates require proportionally longer warmup within the tested regime. Third, batch size controls the late-stage noise scale: smaller batches lead to wider basins, larger batches to deeper ones, and batch-size ramping can maintain steady loss reduction with fewer consumed tokens. The comparison between batch-size ramping and learning-rate decay supports the η/B interpretation, as both reduce the effective noise scale and can yield similar performance trends.19a:T4e3,The work defines a use as one gradient computation reading a rounded tensor. A backward-state policy assigns a value to every such use. The reference is the gradient of the computation that actually produced the loss, with rounding handled by a straight-through convention. Under this reference, each use must read the value used by the corresponding forward operation, or a substitute that gives the same gradient in expectation conditional on the realized forward computation and the incoming gradient received by that use. This conditional requirement is the crucial step: an incoming gradient may depend on the realized rounding, so two values sampled from the same rounding distribution need not be interchangeable. The attention correction term D = rowsum(dO ∘ O) is used as the main example. If dO depends on the forward rounding of O, then reusing that rounded O and drawing a fresh rounding from the same distribution can produce different training behavior. The paper also shows that one tensor can require different values for different gradients, for example in normalization and in rounded attention probabilities. The proposed per-use requirements are then checked with an executable finite-case checker for concrete operator policies.19b:T4b5,The experiments are built around 390M-parameter training runs and low-precision attention backward. In the FOG 390M setting, NVIDIA Transformer Engine FP8 attention fails in all three seeds tested. Replacing only the backward with BF16 while keeping the FP8 forward removes the failure, isolating the issue to the backward policy. In paired runs with an emulated FP8 attention backward, the forward randomly rounds the attention output O. Training fails when the D term reuses the forward-rounded O, but succeeds when D reads a fresh rounding from the same distribution; this is repeated in three paired 390M runs. The two choices have the same copy accuracy, so the difference comes from the dependency between the realized rounding and dO. Another experiment shows that final loss is not enough: a policy that lets the next layer consume the rounded output while both gradients read the original can end with loss inside a pre-specified margin of the reference policy, even though it violates the per-use reference. Predictions about reuse effects are also registered and tested on three PyTorch and Transformer Engine operators, and all predictions match, including cases where reuse should not matter.19c:T880,The paper has two technical pillars: a lower-bound construction and matching upper-bound analysis. The lower bound is the conceptual center. The authors build a rank-one gradient example with unequal row magnitudes. In that setting, Muon’s polar-factor update remains well aligned with the gradient, whereas NorMuon’s row-wise renormalization equalizes row magnitudes but rotates the update away from the gradient. That is the key mechanism: better neuron-wise balance can come with worse descent alignment. The authors then embed this mechanism into a smooth objective whose gradient stays effectively constant along the iterate path, isolating the directional distortion caused by row normalization from other training effects. This yields an algorithm-dependent lower bound of Ω(mLε^-2) iterations for NorMuon to reach an ε-stationary point, compared with Muon’s O(Lε^-2) rate in the same geometry.

The upper-bound side shows the m factor is not merely a proof artifact. The paper proves O(mLε^-2) in the deterministic setting and O(mLε^-2 + m^2Lσ^2ε^-4) in the stochastic setting, with noise measured through a nuclear-norm variance bound. Importantly, the analysis explicitly accommodates approximate polar computation and fixed-parameter EMA momentum. Even with exact polar computation and arbitrary fixed momentum parameters, the dimension-dependent penalty remains. That makes the result structurally stronger: the slowdown is tied to the normalization step itself.

Relative to prior work, the distinction is sharp. NorMuon motivated row normalization through neuron-wise balancing and mitigation of low-leverage rows receiving persistently tiny updates. This paper does not dispute that empirical mechanism. Instead, it shows that balancing update magnitudes and improving convergence are different objectives. The analysis shifts attention from per-row magnitude fairness to update-gradient alignment under operator-norm geometry. That framing is also useful when comparing related variants such as Muon+, MuonEq, and other matrix-aware optimizers: are they changing update magnitudes, update directions, or both, and what is the cost of each choice?19d:T5b5,The experiments are designed to expose the theory–practice gap rather than to maximize benchmark coverage. There are two main parts. First, synthetic optimization problems reproduce the theoretical mechanism: on controlled tasks aligned with the lower-bound construction, NorMuon is slower than Muon, confirming that row normalization can indeed hurt optimization speed when directional distortion dominates. Second, in LLM pretraining, NorMuon outperforms Muon. That contrast is the puzzle highlighted by the title.

The most important empirical takeaway is therefore not a single headline number but the coexistence of three facts: the worst-case complexity of NorMuon carries an extra m factor; this penalty is visible on synthetic tasks; and NorMuon can still be better in realistic pretraining. That strongly suggests its practical gains come from training-specific effects such as improved neuron activity balance or better interaction with real gradient statistics, not from a uniformly better smooth-optimization rate.

The explicit quantitative results stated in the paper include: a lower bound of Ω(mLε^-2) for NorMuon, a deterministic upper bound of O(mLε^-2), a stochastic upper bound of O(mLε^-2 + m^2Lσ^2ε^-4), and Muon’s comparison rate of O(Lε^-2). The provided full-content excerpt does not include detailed pretraining-scale numbers such as model size, token count, or exact validation-loss deltas, so those should not be inferred.19e:T4d8,If reading selectively, start with the introduction’s claim that balanced neuron updates do not imply faster convergence. That is the right lens for the whole paper. Then go to the lower-bound section and study the rank-one unequal-row construction carefully. The key idea is not complicated once isolated: row normalization fixes row imbalance but weakens gradient alignment. Also pay attention to how the authors embed this into a smooth objective with nearly constant gradients along the trajectory; that is what turns an intuitive geometric observation into a rigorous lower bound.

After that, read the experimental comparison between synthetic tasks and LLM pretraining. The paper is strongest when read as an explanation of why both results can be true at once. For deeper study, focus on three questions: what properties of real LLM gradients make row normalization beneficial despite the worst-case penalty; whether the m factor is sensitive to width, sparsity, or training schedule; and whether one could design conditional or selective row normalization that activates only when low-leverage rows are actually suppressed. A quick skim takes 30–45 minutes. A careful read of the proofs and appendices likely needs 2–3 hours.19f:T4e8,The paper uses Partial Information Decomposition to separate multimodal information into four channels. Redundant information R is accessible from either modality. Unique information U_1 and U_2 is accessible only from modality 1 or modality 2. Synergistic information S is accessible only when both modalities are present together. The proposed scaling law writes data loss as a sum of four independent power-law curves. Each curve receives only the relevant data stream: R can be reduced by either modality, U_1 by modality 1 data, U_2 by modality 2 data, and S only by the paired count n_p. This differs from prior L(N, D_1, D_2) forms because it gives paired data its own causal role rather than folding it into modality counts. The experimental protocol is built to isolate this variable. Unpaired examples are represented by a learnable null vector plus a modality-presence bit. At test time, both modalities are always present. Cross-entropy is the main loss, with accuracy checked separately. The main sweeps fix architecture and parameter count, folding finite-model effects into E_N, while appendices repeat Digits and VQA under different architectures and parameter sizes to check that the qualitative conclusions are not tied to a single model.1a0:T5ca,The paper evaluates three settings. Digits combines MNIST images and AudioMNIST spectrograms in a four-digit classification task where the four positions correspond to U_1, U_2, R, and S, giving explicit control over the information channels. VQA trains classification heads on top of frozen pretrained embeddings; this setting is dominated by the text modality and is useful for observing how unpaired data helps non-synergistic information. NLVR2 finetunes a pretrained multimodal transformer on a task where mutual information is largely synergistic and unimodal models remain near chance. Across settings, the authors sweep total data D, compute budget C, paired count n_p, and multiple random seeds. They count D as D_1 + D_2, the sum of unique examples per modality. As p approaches 1, the number of unique rows decreases; training steps are fixed, so fully paired data sees more epochs but the same number of gradient updates. This counting convention favors unpaired data, making improvements from higher p more attributable to pairing itself. The main findings are consistent: pairing ratio has a large effect on loss; laws without p cannot capture the observed curves; only paired data reduces synergistic loss; unpaired data reduces redundant or unimodal loss only up to the relevant floors; and synergy shows a threshold-like acquisition pattern. The provided text does not include exact fit-error numbers for the proposed law, so no additional numeric claims are added.1a1:T42e,The authors study an online teacher-student model with a single softmax layer trained by cross-entropy. Inputs are sampled from an isotropic Gaussian and RMS-normalized, mirroring hidden states before an LM head. A fixed teacher matrix produces hard one-hot labels from the argmax of its softmax output. The student learns with different optimizers. The setup preserves the key nonlinearity behind peaked distribution learning: reducing loss requires both growing the student weight norm, which sharpens the output distribution, and aligning the student direction with the teacher. The analysis decomposes the loss into a radial channel, controlled by norm growth and softmax saturation, and a tangential channel, controlled by directional misalignment. These channels decay with exponents α_r and α_t. SGD places both near one third. Adam produces a different dynamic regime, with α_r near one half and α_t near zero. Across seven optimizers, the exponents obey the relation 2α_r + α_t = 1, which yields the same tuned data scaling L*(D) proportional to D^{-1/3}.1a2:T597,The setup treats a benchmark as a fixed list of M questions. For each question, generated answers have a verifier score S and a correctness bit Y. At budget k, the selected answer is the one with the highest verifier score among k samples, and the curve reports the average correctness over the fixed question list. The audit may adaptively choose questions, extend answer paths, query correctness labels, and stop when it can return a simultaneous confidence band with half-width ε and failure probability δ. The analysis counts three resources: generated answers, correctness queries, and question visits. For a fixed list, the main cost law for certifying all budgets up to K is, up to logarithmic factors, K/ε + min(M, ε^{-2}) + s/ε^2. The three terms correspond to rare high-scoring answers at large budgets, the identity of the benchmark questions, and within-question variance accumulated along the curve. Matching lower bounds show that these terms are intrinsic. A key technical device is a coupling of nested winners on one answer path, which lets a single path serve all budgets. The practical algorithm is a paired audit: each round draws two fresh paths per question, uses an exponential inequality for paired Bernoulli draws to build anytime-valid simultaneous bands, and then applies a corrected exact-binomial final look to stop at a fixed round. Combined with a multilevel audit, it attains near-minimax cost.1a3:T45b,The empirical study uses 185 held-out score pools. The curves often plateau early: the median curve is within 1/32 of its best value by k=10, so small differences matter. On 100 MMLU-Pro questions, a fixed exact-binomial design needs 192,000 generated answers to certify all budgets up to K=64 within ±1/32 at 95% confidence. By contrast, one path of 64 answers per question uses only 6,400 answers and gives unbiased estimates of all points, but does not provide a sufficiently tight simultaneous guarantee. At budget 64, roughly three quarters of the variance in selected-answer correctness comes from between-question variation, which explains why balanced revisits to every fixed question can save cost. In experiments, the paired audit uses 0.74, 0.66, and 0.53 times the generated answers of the cheapest competing certified audit at K=64, 256, and 1024. It is cheaper on all eight generator-benchmark answer sets, misses none of 3,255 runs against exact curves, and its cost follows the three-term theory closely with R^2=0.995. DAG 上的最短路。难点在于，一个词表项一旦被选中，会同时激活它在全语料中的所有 occurrence，因此词表选择和具体分词路径是耦合的。\n\n作者的关键技巧是做 occurrence-level 的拉格朗日松弛：给每个候选 occurrence 一个非负价格 λ_e。这样，文档侧变成“带价格的最短路”，词表侧变成“收集某个 token 在所有 occurrence 上的总 bid”，再减去预算 K 下 top-K bid 的总和，就得到一个全局下界。这个形式有几个优点：一是不需要通用 LP 求解器，核心计算退化为每篇文档的 shortest path 加上全局 token bid 排序；二是价格可以近似优化，但证书有效性可以用独立的整数检查器验证；三是它既适用于 regex-constrained 语料，也适用于 unrestricted 36.8%。这个量级不小，说明预分词边界不是一个轻微工程细节，而是显著限制了压缩最优值。第二，BPE 相对“受边界约束的理论下界”只高 2.1%，说明在固定 regex 约束下，BPE 的压缩效率确实已经接近最优；但相对“无边界的理论下界”则高 10.9%，说明如果把问题定义改掉，BPE 离真正的全局最优并不近。这个结果很好地解释了为什么一边有人说 BPE Diffusion time can therefore encode how much the observed context should be trusted. The work explains why the population-optimal UDM predictor is time-dependent, while time-agnostic predictors can still work well in language-scale finite-data settings.","importance":"The result is useful for diffusion LM design. A hybrid model that enables time conditioning only in that region performs close to a fully time-conditioned model. This is a useful signal for diffusion LM, masked LM, and any-order LM research, where decoding policy can decide whether the training-time parallelism becomes real inference speed.","technical_approach":"Reliable Parallel Decoding is a training-free decoding method. It uses two signals. First, it measures unresolved upstream uncertainty with cumulative entropy over masked upstream positions. If a downstream prediction depends on still-uncertain upstream information, RPD delays it. Second, it identifies tokens that can be committed together using layerwise stability: predictions that remain consistent across the final layers, without losing probability mass, are more likely to be correct. RPD selects candidates using stability and final confidence, then commits them under an entropy budget ordered by upstream uncertainty. This differs from fixed block-wise decoding, whose boundaries do not adapt to the current state, and from confidence or entropy thresholding methods, which score tokens without modeling whether their supporting context has been established.","experiments":"The evaluation uses LLaDA and Dream on mathematical reasoning and code generation, covering four benchmarks and eight model-task settings. One key observation is a U-shaped confidence profile: tokens near the end can look confident because of formatting priors rather than completed reasoning. Enforcing a better commitment order raises accuracy from 57.0% to 62.3% when the answer region is delayed, and to 72.0% when operands are required to precede dependent results. write gate 的训练：当后续 Recall 在正 advantage 轨迹上带来收益时，梯度会穿过 fast-weight memory 回到早先 Think The paper treats redundancy in KV states as a structure that can be exploited, which is a useful lens for long-context model design and evaluation.","technical_approach":"The main method is block-wise low-rank compression of pre-encoded KV caches. MILO does not compress the entire many-shot context as one global matrix, because that can lose fine-grained information and add unnecessary decompression cost. It also avoids per-example compression, which fails to capture shared semantics across examples and can accumulate reconstruction error. Instead, it groups multiple demonstrations into a block and applies low-rank compression at that granularity. A second component is dynamic rank adaptation. Since different blocks have different information density, MILO estimates block entropy and assigns higher rank to high-entropy blocks while compressing redundant blocks more aggressively. The implementation includes custom kernels, CUDA graphs, and stream-level scheduling so that reduced storage translates into end-to-end latency improvements.","experiments":"The reported evaluation uses Qwen2.5 models on standard ICL benchmarks. The key experimental checks are expected to be accuracy under different compression ratios, the effect of block size, fixed-rank versus entropy-adaptive rank allocation, and the latency contribution of the system optimizations. workload、硬件和质量口径下评估。","experiments":"论文给出的关键数字很有用。Llama-3-70B 在 BF16 下权重约 140 GB，已经超过单张 80 GB HBM 加速卡容量。其 KV cache 公式为 Bkv = 2·L·nkv·dh·wkv·s。对 Llama-3-70B，L=80、nkv=8、dh=128、BF16 每元素 2 字节，因此每 token KV cache 为 327,680 字节。单条 128k-token 序列会额外产生约 42 GB KV state；到 10^6 tokens 时约为 328 GB，相当于超过四张 H100 80GB 的总 HBM。算力利用侧，BF16 decode 的权重读取 intensity 约 1 FLOP/B，而 H100 ridge point 约 295 FLOP/B；GQA 即使 group 上，而是记录“已完成的 branch subgraph + 触发它的输入 + 它读过的外部依赖”。后续请求只有在输入精确匹配、且这些外部 reads 仍然新鲜时，才能消费该结果；一旦相关外部状态发生写入，就失效。这解决了 agent 工作流里 retrieval/tool 结果依赖外部环境、不能只靠 prompt exact match 复用的问题。\n\n第二层是 unresolved low-bit quantization of recurrent states in hybrid language models. Unlike ordinary activations or KV entries, errors in recurrent states persist and affect future readouts. Channels with slow decay retain quantization noise for many steps, while fast-decaying channels dissipate it quickly. Uniform range-based quantization therefore allocates precision without considering the future impact of the error.","importance":"The main value for pretraining and architecture work is the connection between hybrid-LM state dynamics and inference-time memory efficiency. Models such as Kimi Delta Attention, Gated DeltaNet, and Mamba-2 replace part of the attention cache with fixed-size recurrent states, shifting the systems bottleneck toward state storage, read/write bandwidth, and numerical precision. The paper provides a data-free, training-free, rotation-free allocation rule for recurrent-state quantization. It also makes a broader point: KV-cache quantization heuristics are not directly sufficient for recurrent architectures, because state errors have temporal dynamics. This can inform future choices of decay parameterization, state grouping, normalization, and quantization-friendly architecture design.","technical_approach":"The method assigns a distortion weight to each state channel using an observability Gramian. Under a local linear noise model, steady-state readout MSE can be approximated as sum_i Gamma_i sigma_i^2, where sigma_i^2 is the quantization noise variance for a row and Gamma_i measures how strongly that row’s error will be observed in future outputs. For diagonal decay without erasure, the paper derives Gamma_i = rho_i / (C expm1(2 s_i)), where s_i is the decay rate, rho_i is query-weighted energy, and C is the write-back interval. Slow decay therefore receives higher precision. These weights are combined with normalized state ranges inside output-normalization groups and plugged into a classical high-rate mixed-precision bit-allocation rule. Decay rates are quantized uniformly in log s, reflecting the sensitivity of long time constants to small relative changes in decay.","experiments":"The experiments evaluate three hybrid models and seven baselines. With per-token recurrent-state quantization, a 4-bit mean payload reduces excess negative log-likelihood by factors of 3.3 to 27.9 relative to the best baseline. At 6 bits, the NLL gap to the FP32-state baseline is below 0.005 nats. The paper includes ablations separating the contributions of variable bit widths, decay-aware weighting, range normalization, and logarithmic decay-rate quantization. It also reports an important caveat: deterministic rounding at C=1 can create correlated errors. In simulations using Kimi-like decays and rank-one writes, lag-one error correlations reach 0.23 for very slow channels, and three-to-five-bit readout error can range from 0.17x to 2.4x the independent-noise prediction. By six bits, discrepancies are typically within 20%. For intermediate Transformer blocks, it minimizes the MSE between quantized and full-precision block outputs; for the final block, it uses KL divergence over the output distribution. Before quantizing each block, it refreshes both gradient and Hessian estimates using backward passes through that block, avoiding the stale-curvature issue in global-objective PTQ methods that compute Fisher or Hessian information only once. For the first-order term, it computes exact gradients instead of relying on the Taylor-style approximation used by FOEM. A trust-region scaling mechanism bounds the gradient compensation step, which is important because first-order corrections can otherwise induce large and unstable weight updates. The paper also derives efficient Hessian approximations for the block-wise objectives and keeps the computational complexity at the same order as vanilla GPTQ, O(max{d_col^3, d_row·d_col^2}).","experiments":"The evaluation covers multiple model families and compares against GPTQ, QuIP, global-objective PTQ variants, and FOEM-like first-order methods. The main reported pattern is that G²PTQ stays closer to the full-precision model in output distribution, with lower KL divergence, and this translates into better downstream task accuracy. A useful systems number is included: quantizing an 8B model takes about 2.24 hours and 12.54 GB of memory on a single accelerator. The ablations focus on the individual roles of first-order compensation, refreshed Hessian/gradient estimates, block-wise supervision, and trust-region scaling.","reading_guide":"Skim the Introduction and Preliminaries first to understand how the paper separates the weaknesses of GPTQ, global-objective PTQ, and FOEM. Along time, every decoding step updates an already quantized state and quantizes it again; retention gates can carry old errors forward. Along space, errors in different key rows have different impact on the output, while state magnitudes vary across both rows and columns. QK logits 项，因此作用路径更单一，但对 logits 更敏感。论文在六个模型、四个家族上做 matched reconstruction error 对比，发现同等缓存重建误差下，RoPE 路径造成的 attention-output distortion 更大。随后给出 operator–error model，从三个角度解释这种放大：注意力对 logits 的敏感性、量化误差能量在不同子空间的分配、以及误差方向与算子主敏感方向的耦合。\n\n第二步是 function-aligned dual-path quantization。核心不是统一做一个量化器，而是为两条路径分别构造“可离线融合”的变换空间，再用不同的功能目标优化。对 content path，目标是 attention-output reconstruction，也就是让量化后的 content latent 在真实 attention 计算后尽量重建输出，而不是只重建 latent 本身。对 RoPE path，目标是 positional QK reconstruction，直接约束位置相关的 QK 项，因为这一路误差主要通过 logits 进入输出；论文还给出了从该目标到输出失真的理论上界。这里的关键判断是：路径结构决定可做哪些 offline-fusible transform，功能误差链路决定该优化什么目标。\n\n第三步是系统实现。作者实现了 native low-bit MLA attention kernel，把 unpack 和 dequantization 融进 attention kernel，而不是先还原成高精度再算。这样做减少额外带宽和中间张量开销，才能把缓存压缩真正转成端到端吞吐收益。论文还在 vLLM 场景下评估了同一调度策略下的 whole-job throughput，而不是只报 kernel microbenchmark。","experiments":"实验覆盖四个 MLA 模型家族，文中前面分析部分提到跨六个模型、参数规模从 16B 到 1T total parameters 的误差特性验证。结果层面，最重要的是三点。\n\n第一，论文声称实现了首个在 content cache 和 RoPE cache 上同时做 INT4 caching、且精度退化很小的方案。相比已有只压 content、不压 RoPE 的做法，这是主要结果。第二，在更激进的设置下，把 content cache 进一步压到 INT2，同时保留 RoPE 为 INT4，在 reasoning 和 code benchmark 上仍保持有竞争力的性能，说明 content path 的可压缩性显著高于 RoPE 级专家分数；最后在预算约束下选择分数最高的专家加载。\n\n论文还处理了一个工程上必须面对的问题：某个 token 路由到的专家如果没被 batch 选中怎么办。这里使用 backfill 机制，用已加载专家中次优候选补位，避免 token 完全失去对应专家路径。实现上作者写了自定义 GPU kernel，把打分、选择和执行流程接到实际解码路径里。与 SERE、OEA 这类从 token token 上限。这样做不是为了省算力，而是为了让后面的“语义压缩提示”只在局部、语义相对一致的范围内工作，避免整篇文档过长时重要性估计过于噪声。\n\n第二步，在每个 chunk 末尾追加一个很短的 semantic compression prompt，例如 “Brief summary: \\\"”。这个 prompt 的作用不是生成摘要文本，而是诱发模型在预测 prompt 后续 表征；二，每个 prompt 只能 attend 自己所属 chunk 的 token，不能跨 chunk 汇总。这样得到的 attention 分布更像“局部压缩时哪些 token 被认为重要”，而不是全局混杂后的注意力。\n\n第四步，用这些 prompt 诱发出的 attention 分布估计 token importance，选出信息量更高的 token，再从一个中间层抽取这些 token GPTQ is sequential: quantizing one input column changes the compensated state of later columns. NVFP4, however, assigns one E4M3 block scale to every 16 E2M1 weights. If a scale is scored only on the initial block values, the score can disagree with the final reconstruction error produced after GPTQ compensation. The second problem is scalability: for 70B–400B-class models, full-precision weights, calibration activations, and second-order state cannot all reside on accelerators at once.","importance":"The contribution is mainly in low-bit inference, but it matters for foundation-model evaluation and release pipelines. Many large checkpoints are evaluated or served in 4-bit-like formats, and poor reconstruction can distort model comparisons. The work is useful because it treats the quantization format, GPTQ’s second-order recurrence, and large-model memory constraints as one coupled problem. It is not a pretraining recipe, but it helps reduce deployment-side artifacts when studying very large models.","technical_approach":"The algorithm, Schur Replay, is a recurrence-aware scale-selection method for NVFP4. GPTQ uses a calibration Hessian H=XX^T and quantizes columns sequentially, compensating future columns after each rounding decision. Since output rows are independent under the same input Hessian, each row follows its own recurrence. For each hardware-valid block scale, Schur Replay replays the GPTQ updates that this candidate scale would induce, then scores the block with a conditional Schur objective that accounts for the remaining compensation available from unquantized columns. This differs from static block-scale search, which evaluates scales before the candidate has changed the GPTQ state. The systems design exploits row independence: rows of the same weight matrix are split across tensor-parallel ranks, only the active layer is kept on device, calibration activations are tiered across device, host, and disk, and full-precision layers are retired after recoverable NVFP4 export.","experiments":"The reported quality results cover Qwen3.5-397B-A17B and Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct across seven benchmarks, with 99.35% / 100.84% recovery relative to BF16. On the 397B model, the infrastructure reports measured per-layer compute speedups of 15.17× / 23.14× over ModelOpt / LLM Compressor at about 35.0GB peak memory per GPU. inference. Key errors perturb query-key scores, while value errors perturb the attention output and the following output projection. Quantizing KV vectors using only their own distribution misses these downstream sensitivities.","importance":"This is mainly an inference-efficiency paper, but it is useful for base-model research because KV cache memory and bandwidth increasingly constrain long-context deployment. The important idea is product-aware quantization: the transform is designed using both the cached tensor and the computation that consumes it. This is relevant to cache-aware long-context modeling, KV compression during training or distillation, and any architecture where the error metric should be tied to attention computation rather than raw vector reconstruction.","technical_approach":"WUSH-KV adapts the WUSH transform to KV caches. WUSH builds a closed-form invertible transform from the Gram matrix of the quantized factor and a Hessian induced by the other factor in a matrix product. For KV cache, the method builds separate transforms for keys and values. The key transform uses calibration statistics of keys and sensitivity from the query heads that consume them. The value transform uses value statistics and sensitivity from the output-projection blocks. The value-side transform can be folded into model weights, so it adds no online transform cost. The key-side transform and query compensation are applied after headwise normalization, when present, and after RoPE, matching the actual attention-score path. The transform is independent of the scalar quantizer and can be paired with clipped per-token quantizers. The method also keeps sink and recent cache entries in full precision to avoid damaging positions that carry disproportionate attention mass.","experiments":"The reported experiments show lower layerwise attention reconstruction error and lower perplexity than existing KV-cache quantization methods. In 2-bit downstream evaluation, WUSH-KV scores above OSCAR on all four Qwen3-8B tasks, and remains competitive on 4B and 32B models. The theoretical analysis focuses on QuEST INT and shows near-optimality of the ideal WUSH transform under an additive rounding-noise model plus assumptions on normalized tails and clipping errors. The provided content does not expose exact perplexity values, task scores, or latency numbers, so the main items to verify are calibration size, group size, number of full-precision sink/recent tokens, transform overhead, and whether memory savings translate into end-to-end throughput gains.","reading_guide":"Skim in 25–35 minutes. useful.","importance":"The work is directly relevant to inference efficiency and also touches the broader question of how diffusion-style language models can support autoregressive generation. Its main lesson is that a non-autoregressive drafter does not have to be a one-shot block predictor. It can draft first and then edit the proposal bidirectionally before target verification. For training, the acceptance objective matters: optimizing a drafter only for independent token accuracy is less aligned with speculative decoding than training it to preserve correct tokens and repair errors in partially correct proposals.","technical_approach":"DEdit is a diffusion-based drafter with two stages. It first generates a full proposal from masked inputs, similar to DFlash. It then performs iterative token-to-token editing over the whole proposal. During editing, every position can attend to bidirectional proposal context, so later candidate tokens can help repair earlier mistakes before the target model verifies the final proposal. The target model and the standard prefix-verification protocol remain unchanged, so improvements appear as a higher expected number of accepted tokens per round. The training method, ProposalMix, constructs proposal-like inputs by mixing first-pass draft predictions with ground-truth tokens according to confidence. This creates realistic partially correct drafts: some tokens should be preserved, while others should be revised. Compared with causal correctors such as Domino, the key difference is access to future proposal tokens during correction.","experiments":"The paper evaluates DEdit with Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B target models under greedy and stochastic decoding across seven benchmarks. DEdit reports the highest macro-average token acceptance among the compared drafters for both targets. Wider proposal windows benefit more from editing: increasing the window from 16 to 32 tokens raises DEdit acceptance by 10.3%, compared with 2.1% for DFlash. ProposalMix reduces harmful edits, roughly halving the number of rounds in which editing shortens the accepted prefix. Controlled context ablations show that future proposal context is important: hiding later tokens lowers acceptance on every evaluated task. The advantage is larger on more predictable outputs, including reasoning, summarization, and a synthetic copy-heavy task, with the largest gain on the copy-heavy setting. In the reported CUDA Graph drafting plus eager target-verification setup, DEdit reaches 5.72× speedup on Qwen3-4B and 5.97× on Qwen3-8B under greedy decoding.","reading_guide":"A skim takes about 30–40 minutes; the method and ablations are worth deeper reading for anyone working on speculative decoding. 上，而不是新的模型架构。","technical_approach":"方法由两个互补组件组成。第一是 Anchor-Label Relabelling，简称 ALR。它不再机械使用原始 corpus token 作为每个 slot 的监督标签，而是以 target model 的 greedy rollout 为锚点，对 block 中各位置重新赋标签分布。这样做的目的，是把已经 上下文，而不是 target 自己会到达的上下文。IRA 直接把 draft blocks 插入 target rollout 内部，让 drafter 在 target-generated context 上训练，并复用前缀计算。这样既减少 train-test mismatch，也提高训练效率。\n\n从全文描述看，作者把 erase 视为强基线，而不是稻草人。erase 来自 PARD-2 The broader lesson is useful beyond decoding: when training data comes from trajectories that do not match the target policy, simply dropping mismatched positions throws away a lot of signal. Rollout-based relabelling can recover that signal. accurate on average. It asks a stricter question: can a low-precision fast matmul realization break prefix invariance in causal LMs? In a linear layer, rows of the activation matrix correspond to token positions. Fast algorithms such as Strassen mix rows across blocks and rely on exact cancellation of cross terms. Under low-precision quantization and rounding, those cancellations may fail, so later-token information can leak into earlier-token outputs. That violates prefix invariance: logits at a position should depend only on the allowed prefix, not on future text. This matters directly for likelihood-based multiple-choice scoring, packed inference, and any setting where one assumes row-local causal semantics. The core problem is therefore how to detect and construct low-precision fast matmul realizations that preserve the multiplication savings while provably retaining the row-local behavior of the classical operator.","importance":"For foundation-model research, the contribution matters in three ways. First, it exposes a failure mode that standard metrics can miss. Accuracy and perplexity do not certify prefix invariance. A kernel can look acceptable by ordinary task metrics and still change likelihood-based decisions because of future-token leakage. Second, it reframes numerical stability as a structural correctness issue, not just an error-magnitude issue. For low-precision inference, packed serving, and any cross-request batching scheme, preserving causal isolation is a stronger requirement than keeping average error small. Third, it provides a constructive certification route: instead of hoping rounding errors are small, it builds realizations whose outputs are bitwise identical to classical int8 matmul. Repeated generations on the same benchmark item produce different binary outcomes, so the benchmark score is an estimate of expected performance. Uniformly repeating every item ignores the fact that item-level rollout variances differ: items with pass probability near 0.5 are noisy, while items near 0 or 1 need fewer samples.","importance":"This is an evaluation-method paper with practical relevance to pretraining and post-training loops. The contribution is a statistically better allocation of the same generation budget, yielding tighter estimates without changing the benchmark or model.","technical_approach":"The method, Speculative Evaluation, uses a Hierarchical Bayesian Neyman policy. For item i with pass probability p_i, the rollout variance is p_i(1-p_i). Classical Neyman allocation would assign more samples to higher-variance items if these variances were known. HBN handles the unknown-variance case with a two-stage design. It first runs a small uniform pilot over all tasks, fits a hierarchical Bayesian model to pool noisy success counts, and uses posterior expected sampling variances as allocation scores. It then performs exact positive-integer Neyman allocation for the remaining budget while keeping at least one fresh continuation sample per task. Pilot size and stage weight are chosen before evaluation, and a weighted estimator reuses the pilot without bias. HBN-async adds a systems component: it speculatively launches continuations from partial pilot feedback and retains only requests selected by the final allocation, reducing idle time at the pilot barrier.","experiments":"Across 107 benchmark–checkpoint profiles and average rollout budgets of 8–64 per task, HBN reduces estimator variance by 12.8%–33.6% on average relative to Uniform. This is a useful warning for long-horizon agent evaluation and retrieval-augmented systems: majority agreement and semantic deduplication can both be misleading when sources are correlated.","technical_approach":"CPB has two modes. 下比较两者表现差异。评测协议采用 retrieval 风格，并构造 hard negatives 来定向测试 object、attribute、relation 三种技能。围绕这个测试床，作者提出两类分析。第一类是 compositional integration gap：把 composed caption 与其 decomposed 版本在相同 primitive 集合和相同扰动下比较，测量仅由“需要联合整合多个 primitive”带来的额外损失。第二类是 skill load：把性能建模为 primitive count 的函数，分别看某项技能随着同类 primitive 增多时的 self-load，以及随着其他 primitive 增多时的 cross-load。这个设计比传统 compositional benchmark 更细，因为它不只问“复杂度高时是否失败”，而是问“失败来自哪种 primitive 负载，以及是否真是 joint reasoning 造成的”。","experiments":"实验规模上，作者在 87K image-caption pairs 上分析 compositional integration，在 274K pairs 上分析 skill load，覆盖 object、attribute、relation 三类技能，并评测了多种 VLM，包括标准对比式编码器、显式做 compositional reasoning 的模型、以及非对比式架构。主结论有三点。第一，compositional integration 确实存在稳定成本，也就是 composed caption 相比 decomposed counterpart 会更难，但这个 gap 只解释了总退化的一部分，不足以解释复杂度上升时接近随机的整体崩塌。第二，不同技能对 primitive count 的敏感性不同，而且不仅受自身 primitive 数量影响，也受其他类型 primitive 的 cross-load 影响。换言之，relation 变多不只伤 relation 判断，也可能拖累 object 或 attribute 相关检索。第三，这些模式在不同模型家族中都存在，但幅度和形状不同，说明某些架构或训练目标可能改善了某一类负载，却未必改善真正的组合整合。虽然摘要没有给出具体百分点，全文的价值在于趋势和归因：作者用受控对照证明“组合性失败”不是单一瓶颈，而是 joint integration cost 与 skill-specific load 共同作用的结果。","reading_guide":"泛读建议先看方法图和任务定义。重点是弄清楚 composed vs decomposed 的配对方式，以及 hard negatives 如何分别对应 object、attribute、relation 错误。然后看两组主结果：一组是 compositional integration gap 随复杂度变化的曲线，另一组是 skill load Position bias, transitivity violations, and pairwise agreement treat all comparisons equally, while Bradley–Terry ranking geometry says that close pairs and far-apart pairs have very different effects on recovered rankings. Close pairs are near coin flips; far pairs carry most of the ranking signal.","importance":"The main relevance to foundation-model work is evaluation infrastructure. LLM judges are now used for model selection, preference-data filtering, reward construction, and benchmark aggregation. If reliability metrics are dominated by close-rank-gap pairs, they can penalize judges for uncertainty that has little ranking cost, while missing errors on easy high-gap comparisons that do damage the final ordering. The practical implication is to report judge reliability by pair difficulty or rank gap, rather than relying on aggregate pairwise agreement or raw position-bias rates.","technical_approach":"The analysis uses the Bradley–Terry model. Each item has a latent strength θ, and the probability that item i beats item j is σ(θ_i - θ_j). For a pair with gap Δ, the two possible outcomes differ in log-likelihood by |Δ|. A flipped verdict on a close pair is almost free under the model and barely moves the maximum-likelihood ranking. A flipped verdict on a far pair has a large likelihood cost and pulls the recovered strengths in the wrong direction. This gives a common explanation for run-to-run inconsistency, position bias, and judge-human disagreement. The contribution is not a new judge model, but a reframing of reliability metrics around ranking impact.","experiments":"The controlled simulation fixes pairwise agreement with human labels at 60% and varies only where judge errors occur along the rank-gap spectrum. Judges with the same average agreement produce very different ranking correlations: errors concentrated on large-gap pairs sharply degrade agreement with the gold ranking, while errors on close pairs have much lower cost. The empirical section then studies real pairwise-evaluation data, including 200 texts from the Clear comprehensibility dataset and ASAP 2.0 student-writing data. The experiments stratify inconsistency, position bias, and judge-human disagreement by pair gap, showing that aggregate reliability proxies correlate weakly with human-derived ranking accuracy, while the far-gap tail contains more predictive signal.","reading_guide":"A useful skim takes about 20–30 minutes. Read the Theory section carefully; the key step is the |Δ| likelihood gap between the two outcomes under Bradley–Terry. 标注、支持证据和构造式推理链，但模型答对题，并不等于它真的依赖了这些中间证据。模型可能靠参数记忆、未标注的更短路径、表面线索，甚至局部证据就把答案猜出来。论文用行为干预的方式把这个问题形式化：如果删掉某一跳对应的证据，模型还能答对，那么这一步对该模型并不“行为上必要”。核心问题因此是，如何把“有标注的推理结构”与“模型实际依赖该结构作答”区分开，并据此构造更有诊断性的多跳评测集。","importance":"对基座模型研究的直接价值不在于提出了新的训练方法，而在于它把一个长期被默认接受的评测前提拆开了：answer accuracy 不能直接当作 compositional reasoning 的证据。这个结论对长上下文预训练、检索增强、reasoning data 合成、以及 post-train 阶段的推理能力评估都很重要。若 benchmark 本身允许大量 shortcut，模型在其上的提升就很难解释为“推理能力提升”。这篇工作的贡献量级主要体现在评测方法学：一是提出了可操作的行为审计指标 BNR：只在模型原本答对的样本上统计，随机抽取一个标注 hop 或 support group，删除其对应证据后，如果模型不能再恢复正确答案，则记为该证据对该模型是行为必要的。为了避免“删文本本身就让题更难”这种非特异性影响，作者还设计了 matched-background control，用背景删除对照来分离 evidence-specific failure 和 generic deletion sensitivity。这个设计比单看 accuracy drop 更干净，因为它关心的是‘删掉被宣称必要的那部分证据后，失败是否显著高于删掉长度和位置匹配但语义无关的背景文本’。\n\n第二部分是 RealHop 数据构造框架。它不是简单加 distractor，而是围绕“让每一步都不可绕过”来重写问题与上下文。具体包括三类操作：1）entity verification 分离：先通过结构和语义检查筛样本，冻结数据后，再做 targeted deletion 审计，避免边构造边调 benchmark 到某个模型上。对没有原生 hop 标注的数据，如 FRAMES，作者通过 source-linked evidence 重新建立可干预的支持单元。对 LongBench v2，则进一步把长文档任务改造成可审计的 multiple-choice multi-hop reasoning itself. It asks a more basic question: do current multi-hop benchmarks actually measure dependence on the intended reasoning chain? Existing datasets often provide annotated hops and supporting evidence, and correct answers are commonly treated as evidence that the model composed those steps. The paper shows that this inference is weak. A model may answer correctly via memorized associations, an unannotated shorter path, partial evidence, or superficial cues. The core problem is therefore to separate annotated reasoning structure from behavioral reliance on that structure, and to build benchmarks where each intended step is genuinely necessary for successful answering.","importance":"Its main contribution is methodological rather than algorithmic. For pretraining and foundation-model research, this matters because many claims about reasoning, long-context understanding, retrieval use, or synthetic reasoning data rely on benchmark scores whose diagnostic validity is often assumed rather than tested. The paper argues that answer accuracy alone is not sufficient evidence of compositional reasoning. It contributes a behavioral auditing metric, BNR, and a benchmark construction pipeline, RealHop, that makes evidence necessity measurable and enforceable. The practical impact is that benchmark scores become more interpretable, and model differences become more separable once shortcut paths are removed.","technical_approach":"$9c","experiments":"$9d","reading_guide":"For a skim-level read, start with the introduction and problem formulation. It introduces a simple intervention: generate the rationale before the answer, or generate the answer before the rationale, while keeping the task and prompt structure controlled.","importance":"The work is mainly an evaluation and diagnostic study for VLM reasoning faithfulness, with indirect relevance to pretraining and post-training. The useful idea is that generation order changes the autoregressive conditioning structure. In rationale-first generation, the answer can condition on the explanation. In answer-first generation, the explanation is more likely to be a post-hoc justification. This matters for rationale supervision, CoT-style data construction, and multimodal instruction tuning.","technical_approach":"The method has two components. The first is a generation-order intervention comparing rationale-first and answer-first prompting under a shared structured-output format, implemented with JSON for reliable parsing. The second is explanation-supervised fine-tuning. For each example, the authors construct two target sequences using the same answer and rationale: R*→A* and A*→R*. The rationales are produced post hoc while conditioning on the ground-truth answer, so the supervision is answer-consistent and less noisy than free-form intermediate reasoning. Training uses the standard autoregressive likelihood over both sequence orders.","experiments":"The experiments use 7B-scale VLMs: Qwen-2.5-VL-7B-Instruct and LLaVA-1.5-7B. The evaluation covers three visual-language reasoning datasets spanning knowledge-intensive VQA, visual grounding, and world-knowledge inference. The provided text does not expose the full numerical tables, so the safe summary is methodological: the key measurements are accuracy, consistency, and output stability under RF versus AF, in both zero-shot and fine-tuned settings. It also frames some VLM failures as evidence-binding and representational-interference problems, rather than pure perception failures. This is relevant to native multimodal pretraining and visual tokenization, where the structure of intermediate representations matters.","technical_approach":"NeuronEye has three components. Sparse Neuron Space trains a sparse autoencoder on frozen intermediate vision-token activations. A d-dimensional patch state is projected into an overcomplete latent space D=αd, followed by ReLU sparsification, and the resulting neurons are clustered into concept-level groups. Neuron-guided Visual Focus uses both the text query and image-side evidence to select relevant clusters, localize the patches where these concepts are expressed, and inject the activated evidence back into the corresponding vision tokens. Perceptual Concept Suppression is applied at a later layer to attenuate dominant perceptual directions, so that focused activation does not wash out weaker but relevant cues. The difference from token pruning or generic representation steering is that the intervention is routed through a sparse concept vocabulary. The VLM backbone and the SAE remain frozen, and inference is still a single forward pass.","experiments":"The evaluation covers four vision-centric benchmarks and two backbones. Similar trends are reported on LLaVA-1.6-7B, especially on spatial and relational subtasks. Visual understanding often uses ViT semantic features, while visual generation often uses VAE reconstruction latents. The same image can therefore consume two visual streams, increasing context length and complicating pretraining pipelines. The paper explores whether raw pixel patches and video tubelets can serve as a shared interface for both understanding and generation.","importance":"The main relevance for pretraining research is the visual interface. PixelUMM does not replace a VAE with another learned autoencoder; it removes the latent encoder stage and connects pixels directly to the multimodal backbone. This reduces the burden of maintaining separate semantic and reconstruction-oriented visual streams, and makes the setup closer to standard single-stream VLM pretraining. The tradeoff is that the backbone must learn semantic abstraction and fine-detail preservation from raw pixels, making patch size, decoder design, and staged training more important.","technical_approach":"The model uses an encoder-free pixel interface. Images are partitioned into non-overlapping 2D patches, while videos are partitioned into spatiotemporal tubelets. The reported default is p=16 for image patches and τ=4, p=16 for video tubelets. Each flattened patch or tubelet is mapped to the Transformer hidden dimension through a single linear layer. Clean visual inputs use understanding projections; corrupted generation targets use separate generation projections. The output side uses RMSNorm followed by a linear projection back to pixels, then unpatchifies the predictions. Output projections are zero-initialized before multimodal training. The backbone uses a Mixture-of-Transformers design with shared multimodal attention and separate parameters for understanding and generation. Training combines autoregressive text prediction with pixel-space flow matching, and follows a staged recipe that progressively adds image tasks, video tasks, and higher spatial resolutions.","experiments":"The paper reports competitive results across image understanding, image generation, video understanding, and video generation. If an early spatial interpretation is wrong, later reasoning often inherits that error.","importance":"The paper is mainly a post-training and reasoning-representation contribution. Its relevance to pretraining research is that token sequences may be a poor carrier for some intermediate reasoning states. Spatial reasoning often involves several plausible object or relation hypotheses. Continuous intermediate states can keep alternatives alive before a final discrete answer is produced. The work does not change the pretraining objective, but it is useful for thinking about latent reasoning, soft CoT, and how post-training shapes internal reasoning trajectories.","technical_approach":"The method replaces hard intermediate CoT tokens with soft states. At each reasoning step, the model forms a weighted mixture of candidate token embeddings instead of selecting a single token embedding. This continuous state conditions the next step. The AdaptSoft controller adjusts the softness of the mixture using the current hidden state and predictive uncertainty. This matters for spatial tasks because some steps benefit from maintaining several plausible scene interpretations, while other steps require a sharper commitment. For training, the method uses GRPO: for each image-query pair, it samples a group of rollouts and assigns answer and format rewards. It further adds Gradient-Alignment Learning, which compares each step’s policy-gradient contribution with a reference gradient to provide step-level credit. This trains both AdaptSoft and the LVLM without intermediate reasoning annotations or an external evaluator.","experiments":"The experiments cover 19 spatial reasoning categories and compare against strong spatial reasoning baselines. The reported result is an overall improvement from adaptive soft thinking. The important experimental message is about control of softness: a fixed level of softness is not appropriate for all reasoning steps. Softer mixtures help when multiple interpretations remain plausible, but excessive softness can mix incompatible relations and hurt subsequent reasoning. The generator update is driven by the difference between a frozen real score model and a trainable fake score model. SAP-DMD inserts a frequency-domain operation on this directional field. It applies a 2D FFT, adaptively suppresses excessive upper-tail amplitudes in the spectrum, preserves the phase, and transforms the field back before applying the update. 共享同一个隐含世界机制，例如相同的摩擦、质量、刚度，同时又允许不同动作带来不同结果。对 world model 用于规划来说，这个约束很关键，因为规划依赖的是“如果我换个动作，世界会怎样变”，而不是若干彼此独立、互相矛盾的想象结果。","importance":"对基座预训练本身的直接影响有限，它更接近物理世界模型和可干预生成建模；但方法上有两个启发。第一，它把“多分支预测之间的一致性”从隐含假设变成了显式训练目标，这对未来做 any-order generation、counterfactual 的分布，而不是输出一个点估计。这样做是为了表达不同干预对物理参数约束强弱不同：强碰撞分支可能把摩擦范围压得很窄，弱扰动分支则只能给出宽后验。第二部分是 shared-world evidence score。论文不是要求各分支 posterior 完全一致，而是相对初始场景先验 p(z|I0) 来衡量多分支是否仍保留对同一机制的共同支持。这个 prior-corrected 去掉外部 teacher，改用同一个初始 checkpoint 的拷贝作为 privileged teacher。teacher 的输入包含题目、ground-truth solution 和 student 当前生成的 prefix；student 只看到题目。这样 teacher 能在 gold-conditioned context 下提供更密集的 token-level clipped objective，clip 参数为 0.2；但消融显示，insight token 上的监督信号才是主要来源。这个设计和普通 self-reflection 的区别在于：reflection 不只是推理时上下文技巧，而是被作为可反传的训练目标写入参数。","experiments":"实验使用 Qwen 3.5 9B Thinking 作为基座 agent，任务是 agentic For a query x and prior history C, the writer produces query-conditioned textual memory M containing relevant evidence, temporal relations, and derived facts. A compressor encodes M through the first four blocks of a frozen backbone and maps it into K continuous vectors Z. The reader generates responses conditioned on x and Z. During on-policy training, the student samples a response under soft memory. A frozen teacher, initialized from the same reader but conditioned on textual memory M, scores the identical token sequence. Token-level log-probability gaps reveal positions where the textual-memory reader is more confident than the compressed-memory reader. A small language model is fit to the data from round t−1 and then used to score both round t−1 and round t data with negative log-likelihood. If the new round has higher NLL under the previous-round model, it contains content that the previous distribution does not explain. Under an exact distributional fit, the quantity decomposes into KL divergence between the two round distributions plus the change in entropy. This separates distribution shift from diversity change. The proposed ATRI module uses the signal in two ways: within a round, samples with above-average information gain receive larger weights; across rounds, training stops when the gain remains below a threshold for consecutive rounds.","experiments":"The paper reports evaluations on several common self-evolution datasets and compares ATRI against filtering- and regularization-based baselines. 的条件概率变化。这样可以避免“换图后模型生成了另一条轨迹”带来的混杂因素。作者定义 EFS 来度量图像干预对 claim token 预测分布的影响强度；如果模型真的在用视觉证据，EFS 应该上升。但仅有 EFS 不够，因为整条轨迹在换图后可能出现全局 likelihood 漂移，所以作者又定义 claim persistence，并用同一 rollout 中的 residual tokens span。对于正 advantage 的 token，如果对应 claim 在反事实图像下能明显 retract，就保留完整正信用；如果 claim 异常 persistent，即证据被破坏后仍维持高支持度，则衰减其正信用。负 advantage token 和非 routed token 不做改动。这样设计很克制：它不直接惩罚所有视觉 token，也不需要 claim 的人工真值标签，只是在“本来会被奖励”的位置上做选择性减弱。作者强调 PACG 可组合到 DAPO、VPPO 这类现有 RLVR 优化器上，而且没有推理时额外开销。\n\n和已有 perception reward、token reweighting、multimodal PRM 的区别在于，这篇工作不主要问“哪些 token 看了图”，而是问“这些 token clipping 从经验技巧重新表述为对 sample-wise policy-gradient coefficient 的直接约束，并把它和 policy mirror descent 里的 gradient clipping 联系起来。对于做 reasoning RL、verifiable reward、甚至 pretrain↔posttrain 接口的人，这个视角是有用的，因为它更接近训练动力学本身：什么样的样本在主导更新，为什么会不稳定，怎样在不显著牺牲样本效率的情况下压住方差。贡献量级上，它属于“把一个常用工程技巧改成更合理的控制变量，并给出一定理论支撑”的工作，偏实用，也有一定方法论价值。","technical_approach":"核心做法很直接。标准 policy gradient 中，单个样本对梯度的贡献系数近似是
